children.title: Routing-Component Decomposition Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Approximation through decomposition into routing substructures.

children.title: Path Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of routing structure into path components.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonnegative flow decomposition into source-sink paths and directed cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed graph and let \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}^{E}\) satisfy flow conservation at every vertex except possibly \(s\) and \(t\), with net outflow \(v\geq0\) at \(s\) and net inflow \(v\) at \(t\). Then there exist directed simple \(s\)-\(t\) paths \(P_i\), directed simple cycles \(C_j\), and positive coefficients \(\lambda_i,\mu_j\) such that \(x=\sum_i\lambda_i\chi^{P_i}+\sum_j\mu_j\chi^{C_j}\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=v\). The number of components can be chosen at most \(|E|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite nonnegative s–t flow is a weighted sum of simple s–t paths and directed cycles, using at most one component per edge.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite directed graph.
\(x\) is nonnegative and conserves flow outside \(s,t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=\sum_i\lambda_i\chi^{P_i}+\sum_j\mu_j\chi^{C_j}\), with positive coefficients and at most \(|E|\) components.

notation.meaning: edge-incidence vector of path or cycle Q

source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models
source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Path Flows and Conformal Decomposition p. 7

source_witnesses.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models
source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Path Flows and Conformal Decomposition p. 7

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive realization of the accepted finite flow-decomposition theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonnegative \(s\)-\(t\) flow \(x\), while its value is positive, find a directed \(s\)-\(t\) path in the positive support, subtract its minimum edge flow, and output the weighted path. The residual then has value zero and is a nonnegative circulation; repeatedly extract bottleneck directed cycles. Every iteration zeros a positive-support edge, so at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(x)|\) components are output. Fresh linear-time searches give \(O(|E|(|V|+|E|))\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bottleneck subtraction extracts source-sink paths and then residual cycles, eliminating a support edge on every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a finite nonnegative source-sink flow of nonnegative value.
Searches use the current positive support.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Elimination Path–Cycle Extraction

children.title: Cycle Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of routing structure into cycle components.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conformal decomposition of a nonnegative circulation into directed simple cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed graph and let \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}^{E}\setminus\{0\}\) be a circulation, so \(\sum_{e\in\delta^+(v)}x_e=\sum_{e\in\delta^-(v)}x_e\) for every \(v\in V\). Then there exist directed simple cycles \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) and coefficients \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m>0\) such that \(x=\sum_{j=1}^m\mu_j\chi^{C_j}\). The decomposition is conformal: every edge used by a cycle has positive \(x_e\), and one may choose \(m\leq|\{e\in E:x_e>0\}|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonzero nonnegative circulation decomposes conformally into positively weighted directed simple cycles, with no more cycles than positive-flow edges.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite directed graph.
\(x\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}^{E}\setminus\{0\}\) satisfies flow conservation at every vertex.

notation.meaning: outgoing and incoming edges at v

source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models
source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Path Flows and Conformal Decomposition p. 7

review_flags: Confirm that the cited subsection explicitly states the circulation-only specialization.

source_witnesses.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models
source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Path Flows and Conformal Decomposition p. 7

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive algorithm for the accepted circulation decomposition theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: While \(x\neq0\), find a directed simple cycle \(C\) in the positive support, set \(\mu=\min_{e\in C}x_e\), output \((C,\mu)\), and replace \(x\) by \(x-\mu\chi^C\). Each iteration preserves nonnegativity and conservation and removes at least one support edge. Thus at most \(|\operatorname{supp}(x)|\) iterations occur; fresh linear-time support searches give \(O(|E|(|V|+|E|))\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly subtracting a bottleneck positive-support cycle constructs the decomposition and eliminates an edge per iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a finite nonzero nonnegative circulation.
A directed cycle is found in the current positive support.

notation.meaning: minimum residual circulation on the extracted cycle

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Elimination Cycle Extraction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extreme Rays of the Nonnegative Circulation Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral characterization of irreducible nonnegative circulation components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite directed graph with node-arc incidence matrix \(B\), let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^E_{\geq0}:Bx=0\}\). The extreme rays of \(K\) are exactly the rays \(\{\lambda\chi^C:\lambda\geq0\}\) generated by directed simple cycles \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The irreducible rays of the nonnegative circulation cone are precisely directed simple-cycle flows.
assumptions_latex: The directed graph is finite.
\(B\) is its node-arc incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ExtRays}(K)=\{\mathbb R_{\geq0}\chi^C:C\text{ is a directed simple cycle}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Rays of the Nonnegative Circulation Cone

children.title: Tour Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition or construction organized around complete tour components.

knowledge_statements.title: Tour Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of a finite closed walk into edge-disjoint simple cycles with multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=(v_0,e_1,v_1,\ldots,e_m,v_m)\) be a finite closed walk in an undirected multigraph, with \(v_m=v_0\). Then the edge occurrences of \(W\), counted with multiplicity, can be partitioned into edge-disjoint simple cycles \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\). Hence \(\chi^W=\sum_{i=1}^q\chi^{C_i}\). For every additive edge cost \(c\), this decomposition also satisfies \(c(W)=\sum_{i=1}^q c(C_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The edge occurrences of any finite closed tour partition into simple cycles, preserving incidence multiplicities and every additive edge cost.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is a finite closed walk in an undirected multigraph.
Edges and costs are counted with traversal multiplicity.
review_flags: The node may intend depot-route splitting rather than closed-walk cycle decomposition.

children.title: Component-Assembly Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Quality loss and feasibility issues arising when routing components are recombined.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed Eulerian boundary for assembling arc components into one closed routing walk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be the directed multigraph obtained from the multiset union of proposed directed path and cycle components after deleting isolated vertices. Its arc occurrences can be assembled without added arcs into one closed directed walk using every occurrence exactly once if and only if its underlying undirected support is connected and \(\deg_D^+(v)=\deg_D^-(v)\) for every vertex \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed components assemble into one arc-exact closed tour exactly when their support is weakly connected and every vertex is balanced.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite nonempty directed arc multiset.
Every arc occurrence must be used exactly once.
No joining arcs may be added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ has a directed Euler tour}\iff D\text{ is weakly connected and }\deg_D^+(v)=\deg_D^-(v)\ \forall v.

notation.meaning: outdegree and indegree with arc multiplicity

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Component-Assembly Criterion
Component-Assembly Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity and parity obstructions to assembling path and cycle components into one tour.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\neq\varnothing\) be the multiset union of proposed undirected path and cycle components on a finite vertex set \(V\), and let \(H=(V,M)\) after isolated vertices are discarded. The components can be spliced using only their existing edge occurrences into a single closed tour traversing every occurrence exactly once if and only if \(H\) is connected and every vertex has even degree. Thus a disconnected support or an odd-degree boundary vertex is an assembly obstruction unless additional joining edges are introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Existing path and cycle components assemble into one edge-exact closed tour precisely when their nonisolated union is connected and all degrees are even.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite nonempty undirected edge multiset.
Assembly must use every edge occurrence exactly once and may add no edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An edge-exact closed tour exists if and only if \(H\) is connected after removing isolated vertices and \(\deg_H(v)\) is even for every \(v\in V(H)\).

notation.meaning: assembled support multigraph after isolated vertices are removed

review_flags: Standard Eulerian assembly boundary, but no matching source locator was supplied.

children.title: Cluster-Partition Decomposition Family
children.top_down_role: Reduction of global structure to approximately separable clusters.

children.title: Cluster-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Approximation through grouping elements into approximately separable clusters.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph decomposition into vertex clusters with explicit internal and boundary edge sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph. A cluster-based decomposition is a family \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_k\}\) of nonempty, pairwise-disjoint subsets whose union is \(V\). For each cluster define \(E_r=\{uv\in E:u,v\in C_r\}\), and define the cross-cluster boundary \(\delta(\mathcal C)=E\setminus\bigcup_{r=1}^k E_r\). The decomposition represents \(G\) by the induced subgraphs \(G[C_r]=(C_r,E_r)\), together with \(\delta(\mathcal C)\); hence every edge is assigned uniquely either to one cluster subproblem or to the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph is split into disjoint vertex clusters; every edge belongs uniquely to an induced cluster subgraph or to the cross-cluster boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected graph.
\(\mathcal C\) is a finite partition of \(V\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard graph-partition definition specialized to constructive decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports this particular cluster-decomposition formulation.

children.title: Partition-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Approximation through division into subinstances with controlled interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of a finite combinatorial instance by a partition of its ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a finite ground set and let \(\Pi=(U_1,\ldots,U_k)\) be nonempty, pairwise-disjoint blocks with \(U=\bigcup_{r=1}^k U_r\). For a set-function objective \(F:2^U\to\mathbb R\), a partition-based decomposition consists of restricted functions \(F_r:2^{U_r}\to\mathbb R\) and an interaction term \(B:2^U\to\mathbb R\) satisfying, for every \(S\subseteq U\), \[F(S)=\sum_{r=1}^k F_r(S\cap U_r)+B(S).\] It is separable precisely when \(B(S)=0\) for every \(S\subseteq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition decomposition expresses every solution value as the sum of block-restricted values and an interaction term; it is separable when that term vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite.
\(F\) is a real-valued set function on \(2^U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact block-plus-interaction decomposition of a set function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-plus-interaction identity is valid once the functions are supplied, but it is highly nonunique and potentially vacuous. A source is needed to establish that this is the intended partition-decomposition concept.

children.title: Cross-Cluster Boundary Effects
children.top_down_role: Approximation losses associated with interactions spanning multiple clusters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Boundary Error Does Not Automatically Give a Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of uniform cross-cluster additive error into a minimization approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|F(S)-\widetilde F(S)|\leq B\) for every feasible \(S\), where \(F\geq0\), and \(\widetilde F(\widehat S)\leq\alpha\widetilde F(S^*)\) for an optimum \(S^*\) of \(F\). Then \[F(\widehat S)\leq\alpha F(S^*)+(\alpha+1)B.\] Hence \(B\leq\varepsilon F(S^*)/(\alpha+1)\) implies \(F(\widehat S)\leq(\alpha+\varepsilon)F(S^*)\). Without a bound relating \(B\) to a positive optimum benchmark, additive boundary control alone implies no finite multiplicative ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary estimate gives additive control and yields a ratio only when the error is small relative to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(\widetilde F\) are nonnegative minimization objectives on the same feasible family.
\(|F(S)-\widetilde F(S)|\leq B\) uniformly.
\(\widehat S\) is an \(\alpha\)-approximate solution for \(\widetilde F\).

notation.meaning: surrogate objective omitting or approximating cross-cluster interactions

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Boundary Error Does Not Automatically Give a Ratio
Cross-Cluster Boundary Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective contribution of edges crossing a vertex-cluster partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) have edge weights \(w:E\to\mathbb R\), let \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_k\}\) partition \(V\), define \(E(C_r)=\{uv\in E:u,v\in C_r\}\), and define \(\delta(\mathcal C)=E\setminus\bigcup_{r=1}^kE(C_r)\). For an edge-additive objective \(F(S)=\sum_{e\in E}w_e\phi_e(S)\), every feasible object \(S\) satisfies \[F(S)=\sum_{r=1}^k\sum_{e\in E(C_r)}w_e\phi_e(S)+\sum_{e\in\delta(\mathcal C)}w_e\phi_e(S).\] Thus, when the same \(S\) is evaluated using only intra-cluster edges, the omitted contribution is exactly the boundary term. If \(|\phi_e(S)|\leq1\) for every \(e\in\delta(\mathcal C)\), its absolute value is at most \(\sum_{e\in\delta(\mathcal C)}|w_e|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any fixed feasible object and edge-additive objective, evaluation using only intra-cluster edges omits exactly the crossing-edge contribution, whose magnitude is bounded by the total absolute boundary weight when each boundary factor has magnitude at most one.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected edge-weighted graph.
\(\mathcal C\) partitions \(V\).
\(F\) is edge-additive.
\(|\phi_e(S)|\leq1\) for every boundary edge when the bound is invoked.

notation.meaning: edges with both endpoints in cluster C_r
edges whose endpoints lie in distinct clusters

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: edge-partition identity and triangle-inequality bound

children.title: Deterministic LP Rounding
children.top_down_role: Deterministic conversion based on fractional solution structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic LP Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic rounding with an explicit approximation certificate relative to an LP bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization integer program with feasible set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), cost \(c\), relaxation \(P\supseteq X\), and an optimal fractional solution \(x^*\in P\), apply a deterministic polynomial-time map \(R:P\to X\). Output \(\widehat x=R(x^*)\) and stop. If the rounding invariant guarantees \(c^\top R(x)\leq\alpha c^\top x\) for every relevant \(x\in P\), where \(\alpha\geq1\), then \(\widehat x\) is feasible and \(c^\top\widehat x\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}\leq\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{IP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic map converts an optimal fractional LP solution into an integral feasible solution while preserving a stated approximation factor against the LP lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq P\) and the problem is a minimization problem.
\(x^*\) is an optimal solution of the LP relaxation.
\(R\) is polynomial-time and satisfies the stated rounding invariant.

source_refs.locator: 5.19 The integer rounding and decomposition properties p. 82

review_flags: generic minimization formulation; problem-specific rounding map remains local

source_witnesses.locator: 5.19 The integer rounding and decomposition properties p. 82

children.title: Randomized LP Rounding
children.top_down_role: Probability-based rounding and feasibility restoration.

children.title: Independent Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families based on independent choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance and multiplicative concentration of the cardinality produced by independent rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mutually independent \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(x_i)\), let \(S=\sum_iX_i\) and \(\mu=\sum_ix_i\). Then \(\operatorname{Var}(S)=\sum_i x_i(1-x_i)\leq\mu\). For every \(\delta\geq0\), \[\Pr[S\geq(1+\delta)\mu]\leq\left(\frac{e^\delta}{(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}}\right)^\mu,\] and for \(0\leq\delta\leq1\), \[\Pr[S\leq(1-\delta)\mu]\leq\exp(-\mu\delta^2/2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selected cardinality has the sum of the Bernoulli variances and obeys the standard multiplicative Chernoff tails.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) are mutually independent.
\(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(x_i)\) with \(x_i\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration for Independent Bernoulli Rounding
Independent Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise Bernoulli rounding of a fractional vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in[0,1]^n\), independently sample \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\Pr[X_i=1]=x_i\) for each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and output \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\). The procedure terminates after \(n\) samples and preserves every marginal: \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\). Moreover, for every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \[\Pr[X_i=1\text{ for all }i\in S]=\prod_{i\in S}x_i.\] Feasibility of coupled constraints is not guaranteed and must be established probabilistically or restored afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each coordinate is rounded by an independent Bernoulli trial with its fractional value as success probability; marginals are preserved but coupled feasibility may fail.
assumptions_latex: The Bernoulli samples are mutually independent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The independent Bernoulli rounding algorithm and its marginal and product identities are precise and standard, but no citation with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Dependence-Preserving Rounding Family
children.top_down_role: Rounding families preserving selected aggregate relationships.

children.title: Dependent Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding methods using coordinated choices to preserve aggregate structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of pairwise sum-preserving dependent rounding when the original fractional total is nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[0,1]^n\) and \(s=\sum_i x_i\). If \(s\notin\mathbb Z\), append \(x_{n+1}=\lceil s\rceil-s\), apply the sum-preserving pairwise dependent-rounding rule to the augmented vector, and discard the dummy output. The resulting \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\) and \(\sum_iX_i\in\{\lfloor s\rfloor,\lceil s\rceil\}\) almost surely. If \(s\in\mathbb Z\), the dummy coordinate is unnecessary and the total equals \(s\) surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dummy coordinate extends pairwise dependent rounding to arbitrary totals while preserving original marginals and rounding the total to its floor or ceiling.
assumptions_latex: The augmented vector is processed by the immutable pairwise sum-preserving rule.

notation.meaning: dummy coordinate completing the total to its ceiling

knowledge_statements.title: Dummy-Coordinate Extension for Arbitrary Totals
Dependent Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise dependent rounding preserving coordinates in expectation and an integral total.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in[0,1]^n\) with \(\sum_i x_i\in\mathbb Z\), repeatedly choose fractional coordinates \(i,j\). Set \(a=\min\{1-x_i,x_j\}\) and \(b=\min\{x_i,1-x_j\}\). Replace \(x\) by \(x+a(e_i-e_j)\) with probability \(b/(a+b)\), and by \(x-b(e_i-e_j)\) with probability \(a/(a+b)\). Stop when all coordinates are integral and output \(X=x\). Each update makes at least one selected coordinate integral, preserves \(\sum_i x_i\) surely, and preserves every coordinate in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise random transfers make coordinates integral while preserving the total exactly and each original coordinate as a marginal probability.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_i x_i\) is integral.
review_flags: exact dependent-rounding source absent from supplied hints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise-transfer algorithm is internally correct and fits the dependent-rounding leaf, but its specific update rule and guarantees lack a cited source.

children.title: Correlated Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding methods using designed correlations among discrete choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a prescribed-marginal rounding law supported on a specified integral feasible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be nonempty. An \(F\)-valued random vector \(X\) with \(\mathbb E[X]=x\) exists if and only if \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(F)\). Equivalently, there are \(\lambda_z\geq0\) such that \(\sum_{z\in F}\lambda_z=1\) and \(x=\sum_{z\in F}\lambda_z z\); sampling \(z\) with probability \(\lambda_z\) realizes the correlated rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribed marginals are realizable by a distribution supported on feasible integral points exactly when the marginal vector belongs to their convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Support Characterization
Correlated Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint rounding distributions with prescribed marginals and unrestricted dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fractional vector \(x\in[0,1]^n\), a correlated rounding is a random vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) whose law \(\mu\) is a joint distribution satisfying \[\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}^n:z_i=1}\mu(z)=x_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] No product-form requirement is imposed: for some distinct \(i,j\), one may have \(\Pr[X_i=X_j=1]\neq x_ix_j\). Additional correlation constraints may be selected to enforce feasibility or control the expectation of a nonlinear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated rounding chooses an integral vector from a joint distribution with prescribed coordinate marginals, while allowing nonproduct dependence to support feasibility or objective control.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is a probability distribution on \(\{0,1\}^n\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: joint-distribution formulation of correlated rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The prescribed-marginal joint-distribution definition fits correlated rounding, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Marginal-Preservation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rounding families classified by preservation of individual marginal behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-sensitive objective inequalities implied by upper- or lower-preserving coordinate expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) be a randomized rounding of \(x\in[0,1]^n\). If \(\mathbb E[X_i\mid x]\leq x_i\) for every i, then \(\mathbb E[c^\top X\mid x]\leq c^\top x\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\). If \(\mathbb E[X_i\mid x]\geq x_i\) for every i, the reverse inequality holds for every \(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\). Without a sign restriction on c, either one-sided marginal condition alone need not determine an inequality for \(c^\top X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper or lower marginal preservation transfers to the corresponding expected linear-objective inequality for nonnegative coefficients, but not for arbitrary signed coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) is generated conditionally on \(x\in[0,1]^n\).
\(c\in\mathbb R_+^n\) for the stated one-sided implications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb E[X\mid x]\leq x\Rightarrow\mathbb E[c^\top X\mid x]\leq c^\top x,\qquad \mathbb E[X\mid x]\geq x\Rightarrow\mathbb E[c^\top X\mid x]\geq c^\top x.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Objective Consequences of One-Sided Marginals
Marginal-Preservation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or one-sided preservation of coordinate expectations under randomized rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a randomized rounding rule that, for each \(x\in[0,1]^n\), produces a random vector \(X=R(x)\in\{0,1\}^n\). The exact marginal-preservation condition is \[\Pr[X_i=1\mid x]=\mathbb E[X_i\mid x]=x_i\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] An upper-preserving regime replaces equality by \(\mathbb E[X_i\mid x]\leq x_i\), and a lower-preserving regime replaces it by \(\mathbb E[X_i\mid x]\geq x_i\). Under exact preservation, every linear objective is preserved in expectation: \(\mathbb E[c^\top X\mid x]=c^\top x\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized rounding rule preserves marginals exactly when each output bit has conditional expectation equal to its fractional coordinate; exact preservation preserves every linear objective in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) produces \(X=R(x)\in\{0,1\}^n\) conditionally on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb E[X\mid x]=x\implies\mathbb E[c^\top X\mid x]=c^\top x\quad(c\in\mathbb R^n).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: marginal-preservation predicate and linearity of expectation

children.title: Negative-Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rounding families classified by controlled negative dependence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional negative-dependence condition for disjoint coordinate groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random vector \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) is negatively associated if, for every pair of disjoint index sets \(A,B\) and coordinatewise nondecreasing functions \(f\) and \(g\) for which the expectations exist, \[\mathbb E[f(X_A)g(X_B)]\leq\mathbb E[f(X_A)]\mathbb E[g(X_B)].\] For binary coordinates, negative association implies both negative-cylinder inequalities, whereas the cylinder inequalities alone do not imply negative association.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative association requires increasing functions of disjoint coordinate groups to have nonpositive covariance and is stronger than the two cylinder inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) are disjoint.
The displayed expectations exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Association

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-style concentration for sums of binary coordinates satisfying the relevant cylinder inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\{0,1\}\), let \(S=\sum_iX_i\), and let \(\mu=\mathbb E[S]\). If the all-one negative-cylinder inequality holds for every subset, then for \(\delta\geq0\), \[\Pr[S\geq(1+\delta)\mu]\leq\left(\frac{e^\delta}{(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}}\right)^\mu.\] If the all-zero inequality also holds, then for \(0\leq\delta\leq1\), \[\Pr[S\leq(1-\delta)\mu]\leq\exp(-\mu\delta^2/2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The all-one cylinder condition gives the usual multiplicative upper Chernoff tail, and the all-zero condition gives the corresponding lower tail.
assumptions_latex: The all-one cylinder inequality holds for the upper tail.
The all-zero cylinder inequality additionally holds for the lower tail.
knowledge_statements.title: Chernoff Bounds under Negative Cylinders
Negative-Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cylinder inequalities defining negative dependence for rounded binary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) with marginals \(p_i=\Pr[X_i=1]\) satisfies the negative-cylinder condition if, for every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \[\Pr[X_i=1\text{ for all }i\in S]\leq\prod_{i\in S}p_i\quad\text{and}\quad\Pr[X_i=0\text{ for all }i\in S]\leq\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i).\] This regime bounds simultaneous all-one and all-zero events by their independent-rounding probabilities; it does not, by itself, assert full negative association for arbitrary increasing functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative-cylinder dependence requires simultaneous all-one and all-zero events to be no likelier than under independent variables with the same marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) is a random vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Pr[\forall i\in S:X_i=1]\leq\prod_{i\in S}p_i,\qquad \Pr[\forall i\in S:X_i=0]\leq\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i).\]

notation.meaning: marginal probability of coordinate i being one

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard negative-cylinder inequalities used in dependent rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two negative-cylinder inequalities are stated accurately and appropriately distinguished from full negative association, but no direct citation is supplied.

children.title: Post-Rounding Feasibility Restoration
children.top_down_role: Randomized construction followed by feasibility restoration.

children.title: Randomized Alteration
children.top_down_role: Modification of randomized selections to address undesirable outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention guarantee obtained by charging deletion to initially sampled forbidden sets containing the deleted element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the sample-and-delete framework, suppose \(u\) is deleted only to eliminate a currently present forbidden set \(B
i u\). If \(R\) is the initial sample and \(S\) the final set, then \[\Pr[u
otin S\mid u\in R]\leq\sum_{B\in\mathcal B:u\in B}\Pr[B\setminus\{u\}\subseteq R\mid u\in R].\] Under independent initial sampling, \[\Pr[u\in S]\geq p_u\left(1-\sum_{B
i u}\prod_{v\in B\setminus\{u\}}p_vight),\] where the lower bound may be vacuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An element's deletion probability is bounded by a union bound over initially sampled forbidden sets containing it, yielding an explicit survival bound.
assumptions_latex: Initial inclusions are mutually independent with probabilities \(p_u\).
An element is deleted only to eliminate a currently present forbidden set containing it.
knowledge_statements.title: Element-Survival Bound for Sample-and-Delete Alteration
Randomized Alteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent sampling followed by randomized deletion of constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite, let \(p_u\in[0,1]\), and let \(\mathcal B\subseteq2^U\) be forbidden sets for a packing system. First form \(R\subseteq U\) by including each \(u\) independently with probability \(p_u\). While some \(B\in\mathcal B\) satisfies \(B\subseteq R\), select such a \(B\) according to a specified randomized rule and delete at least one element of \(B\) from \(R\). Stop when no forbidden set remains and output \(S=R\). Since every iteration deletes an element, the procedure terminates after at most \(|U|\) alterations and returns a feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample elements independently, then repeatedly delete an element from each surviving forbidden set; at most one deletion per ground element is needed before feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(\mathcal B\) are finite.
Feasibility means containing no member of \(\mathcal B\).
Each repair iteration deletes at least one current element.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical sample-and-alter scheme for packing systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sample-and-delete algorithm is coherent, terminates in at most |U| iterations, and fits randomized alteration, but it lacks a source with a specific locator.

children.title: Feasibility Repair
children.top_down_role: Postprocessing mechanisms that restore required feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic post-rounding repair specified by a violation oracle and decreasing potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rounded object \(y\) in a finite ambient set \(Y\), a feasible subset \(F\subseteq Y\), a violation set \(\mathcal V\), an oracle \(O:Y\to\{\mathrm{feasible}\}\cup\mathcal V\) satisfying \(O(z)=\mathrm{feasible}\) if and only if \(z\in F\), repair maps \(T_v:Y\to Y\), and a potential \(\Phi:Y\to\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), initialize \(z=y\). While \(O(z)=v\in\mathcal V\), update \(z\leftarrow T_v(z)\). Stop when \(O(z)=\mathrm{feasible}\) and output \(z\). If every infeasible \(z\) satisfies \(\Phi(T_{O(z)}(z))<\Phi(z)\), then the algorithm terminates after at most \(\Phi(y)\) updates and outputs an element of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violation oracle repeatedly applies repairs that strictly decrease a nonnegative integer potential; if the oracle reports feasible exactly on F, the process terminates in F after at most the initial potential many updates.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite and \(F\subseteq Y\).
\(O(z)=\mathrm{feasible}\) if and only if \(z\in F\).
Every repair selected for an infeasible object strictly decreases \(\Phi:Y\to\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\).

notation.meaning: violation oracle that recognizes membership in F

children.title: Repair-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Approximation-quality effects associated with feasibility restoration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation composition when feasibility restoration adds cost to a rounded minimization object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\leq\mathrm{OPT}\) be a lower bound for a minimization problem. If a pre-repair object \(Y\) and its feasible repair \(Z\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[c(Y)]\leq\alpha L\) and \(\mathbb E[c(Z)-c(Y)]\leq\beta L\), then \[\mathbb E[c(Z)]\leq(\alpha+\beta)L\leq(\alpha+\beta)\mathrm{OPT}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construction cost alpha times a common lower bound plus expected repair cost beta times that bound yields an alpha-plus-beta minimization guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is feasible almost surely.
\(L\leq\mathrm{OPT}\).
Construction cost and expected repair increment are bounded against the same L.

notation.meaning: common lower bound on the minimization optimum

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Repair Accounting for Minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation transfer when repair retains a fixed fraction of pre-repair maximization value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, suppose a rounded object \(Y\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[f(Y)]\geq\alpha\,\mathrm{OPT}\), and its feasible repair \(Z\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[f(Z)\mid Y]\geq\rho f(Y)\) almost surely for some \(\rho\in[0,1]\). Then \[\mathbb E[f(Z)]\geq\alpha\rho\,\mathrm{OPT}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If rounding attains an alpha fraction of optimum and repair retains a rho fraction in conditional expectation, the repaired maximization solution attains alpha times rho.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is feasible almost surely.
\(\mathbb E[f(Y)]\geq\alpha\mathrm{OPT}\).
\(\mathbb E[f(Z)\mid Y]\geq\rho f(Y)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: conditional expected fraction retained by repair

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicative Retention through Repair
Repair-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective loss induced by repairing a rounded solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a rounded solution with value \(f(Y)\), and let \(Z\) be the feasible result of a repair procedure. Suppose the repair performs random elementary actions \(a\in\mathcal A\), where action \(a\) incurs objective loss at most \(d_a\geq0\), and let \(I_a\) indicate whether it occurs. If \(f(Y)-f(Z)\leq\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}d_aI_a\) almost surely, then \[\mathbb E[f(Z)]\geq\mathbb E[f(Y)]-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}d_a\Pr[I_a=1].\] Thus lower violation probabilities or cheaper repairs translate directly into a stronger expected approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected repaired value is at least the pre-repair expected value minus the sum of each repair cost times its occurrence probability.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is feasible almost surely.
Each repair action has loss bounded by \(d_a\).
The total loss is bounded by the sum of realized action losses.

notation.meaning: indicator that repair action a occurs
upper bound on the loss caused by action a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: expectation bound obtained from an additive repair-loss certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expected-loss inequality follows correctly from the stated almost-sure additive loss certificate and fits the tradeoff leaf, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Structured Formulation Family
children.top_down_role: Stronger formulations encoding local configurations or extended structure.

children.title: Configuration Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations encoding feasible local configurations as formulation elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Column Generation for Implicit Configuration Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical solution method when configurations are too numerous to enumerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve a restricted master LP and obtain dual prices \((y,\alpha)\). For each resource, minimize \(d_{iC}-\sum_{j\in C}y_j\) over \(C\in\mathcal C_i\), adding any configuration whose value is below \(\alpha_i\). If none exists, the restricted-master primal solution and dual prices are optimal for the full configuration LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation alternates between a restricted master and exact resource-wise pricing; absence of a negative-reduced-cost configuration certifies full-LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: Every pricing subproblem is solved exactly.
Every restricted master attains an optimum.
The configuration families are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation for Implicit Configuration Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary for implicitly represented configuration LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every resource-wise pricing problem is polynomial-time solvable in the rational input length, the full configuration LP is polynomial-time solvable through dual separation and the ellipsoid method despite exponentially many columns. Conversely, exact separation of the full dual requires detecting the same resource-wise pricing violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponential configuration LP is polynomial-time optimizable when its exact pricing problems are polynomial-time solvable.
assumptions_latex: The formulation and pricing data are rational and binary encoded.
Pricing is exact.
The resource index set has polynomial encoding size.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing–Optimization Complexity Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual and Pricing Form of the Covering Configuration LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family dual of the immutable covering-style configuration formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the configuration LP \(\min\sum_{i,C}d_{iC}\lambda_{iC}\) with \(\sum_C\lambda_{iC}=1\), \(\sum_{i,C:j\in C}\lambda_{iC}\ge1\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), the dual is \[\max\sum_{j\in J}y_j+\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \alpha_i+\sum_{j\in C}y_j\le d_{iC}\ (i,C),\quad y_j\ge0,\ \alpha_i\in\mathbb R.\] A column has negative reduced cost exactly when \(d_{iC}-\alpha_i-\sum_{j\in C}y_j<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative item prices and free resource potentials form the dual; finding a negative-reduced-cost configuration is the pricing problem.
assumptions_latex: The immutable covering-style minimization formulation is used.
The configuration families are finite.

notation.meaning: nonnegative dual price of item j
free dual potential for resource i

knowledge_statements.title: Dual and Pricing Form of the Covering Configuration LP
Configuration Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Configuration LP for assigning items to locally feasible resource configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite set of resources, \(J\) a finite set of items, and \(\mathcal C_i\subseteq 2^J\) the family of feasible configurations for resource \(i\). A configuration relaxation has variables \(\lambda_{iC}\ge 0\) and constraints
\[\sum_{C\in\mathcal C_i}\lambda_{iC}=1\quad(i\in I),\qquad \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{C\in\mathcal C_i:j\in C}\lambda_{iC}\ge 1\quad(j\in J).\]
For configuration costs \(d_{iC}\), its objective is \(\min\sum_{i,C}d_{iC}\lambda_{iC}\). Each integral feasible solution selecting one configuration per resource embeds by setting its selected variables to one; fractional variables represent convex combinations of locally feasible configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration relaxation mixes feasible local configurations for each resource while coupling those mixtures through global item-coverage constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite.
Each \(\mathcal C_i\) is explicitly given or accessible through an optimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\) is a fractional convex combination of locally feasible configurations satisfying all global coverage constraints.

notation.meaning: weight assigned to configuration C at resource i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Configuration Relaxations leaf and is internally coherent for the displayed covering-style configuration LP, but configuration relaxations have several problem-dependent coupling conventions. No source or inspectable locator supports this particular formulation.

children.title: Extended Formulations
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional formulations exposing additional structural variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimization and Lifting Through an Exact Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational consequence of exact projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), then for every linear objective \(c\), \[\min_{x\in P}c^\top x=\min_{(x,z)\in Q}c^\top x.\] Every feasible extended point projects into \(P\), and every point of \(P\) has a lift in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear optimization over an exact extension has the same value as optimization over its projected polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is an exact extended formulation of \(P\).
The compared optima are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization and Lifting Through an Exact Extension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical characterization of linear extension complexity for nontrivial polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty polytope of positive dimension and let \(S_P\) be a slack matrix formed from a facet description and all vertices. When extension size counts inequalities, \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_+(S_P).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-dimensional polytope's minimum linear extension size equals the nonnegative rank of its slack matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty finite-dimensional polytope of positive dimension.
Extension size counts inequalities; equations are not counted as inequalities.
\(S_P\) uses a facet description and the vertices of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.title: Yannakakis Factorization Theorem
Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral extensions represented through auxiliary variables and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron. An extended formulation of \(P\) is a system
\[Q=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^{n+k}:Ex+Fz\le g\}\]
such that its projection onto the original coordinates equals \(P\):
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^k,\ (x,z)\in Q\}.\]
Its size is conventionally the number of inequalities in the system, with equations either counted separately or replaced by pairs of inequalities under a stated convention. The extension complexity \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\) is the minimum size of any extended formulation projecting to \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation describes a polyhedron as the projection of a higher-dimensional linear system; extension complexity is its minimum inequality count.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real vector space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical role and projection definition fit the leaf, but the record supplies no source for the extended-formulation definition or its equation and inequality counting convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary Variables Alone Do Not Strengthen an Exact Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred because its primary canonical home is the Formulation-Strength Tradeoffs sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two extended systems project to the same polyhedron, they give identical bounds for objectives in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The claim is correct but belongs primarily to comparative formulation strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Variables Alone Do Not Strengthen an Exact Projection

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns higher-dimensional exact projection, lifting, extension size, optimization through lifts, and slack-matrix factorization. The proposed statement comparing the strength of equal projections was deferred to Formulation-Strength Tradeoffs. Configuration-specific masters are likewise excluded.

children.title: Formulation-Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Navigation across representation size, relaxation strength, and rounding utility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Inclusion Need Not Improve Every Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on monotonicity of formulation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\), \(R_1=\operatorname{conv}(X)\), and \(R_2=[0,1]^2\). Then \(R_1\subsetneq R_2\), but for the minimization objective \(c=(1,1)\), both relaxations have optimum zero. Thus strict containment does not imply strict improvement for every objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly stronger relaxation can give the same bound for a particular objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Inclusion Need Not Improve Every Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison for formulations living in different spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_1,Q_2\) be relaxations in possibly different extended spaces and let \(R_i=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i)\). For a minimization problem, if \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \[\min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x\le\min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x\le\min_{x\in X}c^\top x.\] Strength comparisons between extended formulations must therefore use their projections to common variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended formulations are compared by inclusion of projected regions, not raw dimension or row count.
assumptions_latex: Both projections are valid relaxations of the same minimization problem.
The objective uses only the common original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Strength Comparison

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical complexity relation underlying implicit strong formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty rational polyhedron under the standard oracle and bit-complexity model, polynomial-time strong separation and polynomial-time linear optimization are polynomial-time equivalent. Consequently, an exponentially indexed relaxation can remain tractable when it has a polynomial-time strong-separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear optimization and strong separation are polynomially equivalent for rational polyhedra in the oracle model.
assumptions_latex: The polyhedron is nonempty and rational.
The standard encoding-radius and oracle bit-complexity assumptions hold.
Strong separation, rather than heuristic separation, is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization–Separation Equivalence
Formulation-Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic relation between relaxation inclusion, bounds, and integrality gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible integer set for a minimization problem, let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(X)\), and let \(P\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\). For every objective \(c\) whose displayed optima are finite and positive,
\[\min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x\le \min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x\le \min_{x\in X}c^\top x,\]
and hence
\[\frac{\min_{x\in X}c^\top x}{\min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x}\le \frac{\min_{x\in X}c^\top x}{\min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x}.\]
Thus a stronger relaxation cannot worsen the objective-wise integrality gap, although its description or separation problem may require greater computational resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a smaller valid relaxation gives a no-weaker lower bound and a no-larger objective-wise integrality gap, potentially at higher computational cost.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\) are valid relaxations of \(X\).
All three objective values are finite and the relaxation values are positive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion and objective-gap monotonicity claim is standard and matches the leaf, but the record has no citation, leaves the notation gap_c undefined, and appends a computational-resource tradeoff without specifying a representation, separation, or complexity model.

children.title: Iterative Extreme-Point Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Repeated use of extreme-point structure and controlled constraint relaxation.

children.title: Extreme-Point Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding driven by structural properties of relaxation vertices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A locally generic sufficient condition for factor-two extreme-point rounding in covering systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) relax a binary covering family \(X\), let \(c\ge0\), and let \(v\) be an optimal extreme point with \(v\in\{0,1/2,1\}^n\). If the support incidence vector \(\widehat x_i=\mathbf1[v_i>0]\) belongs to \(X\), then \(\widehat x_i\le2v_i\) for every \(i\), and hence \(c^\top\widehat x\le2c^\top v\le2\min_{x\in X}c^\top x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A half-integral optimal vertex whose support is feasible can be rounded upward to a factor-two covering solution.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is an optimal extreme point in \(\{0,1/2,1\}^n\).
The positive support of \(v\) is integer-feasible.

notation.meaning: Incidence vector of the positive support of the extreme point.

knowledge_statements.title: Half-Integral Support-Rounding Criterion
Extreme-Point Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional rounding template exploiting structural properties of LP vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a minimization relaxation \(P\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(X)\), objective \(c\), and a rounding map \(\rho\) defined on vertices of \(P\), solve the linear program and select an optimal extreme point \(x^*\in P\). Output \(\widehat x=\rho(x^*)\in X\). If the vertex-structure lemma for the formulation guarantees
\[c^\top\rho(v)\le \alpha c^\top v\quad\text{for every relevant vertex }v,\]
then the output satisfies
\[c^\top\widehat x\le \alpha c^\top x^*\le \alpha\min_{x\in X}c^\top x.\]
The algorithm stops after one LP optimization and one application of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the relaxation at a vertex and apply a structure-specific rounding map; a vertex-wise cost inequality yields the approximation guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation has an optimal extreme point.
The map \(\rho\) returns an integer-feasible solution and satisfies the stated factor bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate knowledge kind, but the candidate is only a conditional schema: the relevant vertices, dimensions, rounding map, vertex-structure lemma, and domain of alpha are not fully specified. A source tied to a precise extreme-point rounding framework is required.

children.title: Iterative Constraint Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Variants permitting controlled removal or weakening of constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination bound for a fix-or-drop iterative-relaxation execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an iterative-relaxation execution starts with \(n\) unfixed variables and \(m\) droppable constraints, never reactivates a fixed variable or removed constraint, and in every nonterminal iteration fixes at least one variable or removes at least one constraint. Then it terminates after at most \(n+m\) iterations. If each residual LP and progress operation is polynomial-time computable, the complete execution is polynomial-time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent variable fixing or constraint deletion bounds an iterative-relaxation run by the initial number of variables plus droppable constraints.
assumptions_latex: Fixed variables and removed constraints are never reactivated.
Every nonterminal iteration performs at least one permanent fixing or removal.
Each residual operation is polynomial-time computable for the polynomial-time conclusion.

notation.meaning: Initial numbers of unfixed variables and droppable constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Bound from Strict Progress
Iterative Constraint Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic iterative-relaxation scheme with explicit violation budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Start from a linear relaxation with active variables \(U\), active constraints \(\mathcal A\), and an empty partial solution. At each iteration, compute an extreme optimum \(x^*\). Fix every variable whose value is forced to an admissible integral value and update residual right-hand sides. If no variable is fixed, choose a constraint \(a\in\mathcal A\) satisfying a structural drop rule and delete or weaken it with certified violation budget \(\delta_a\). Repeat until all variables are fixed. Output the assembled integral vector \(\widehat x\). If fixing preserves the objective bound and every dropped constraint can accrue at most \(\delta_a\), then
\[c^\top\widehat x\le c^\top x^{(0)},\qquad A_a\widehat x\le b_a+\delta_a.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly fix integral extreme-point variables or relax a structurally safe constraint, yielding an integral solution with certified additive violations.
assumptions_latex: Every nonterminal iteration admits a fixing or drop rule.
Residual LPs remain feasible and attain extreme optima.
Each drop rule supplies a valid violation budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\) is integral, respects retained constraints, and violates each relaxed constraint by at most its certified budget.

notation.meaning: allowed additive violation for constraint a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the iterative-constraint-relaxation leaf, but the active LP, admissible fixing values, residual update, structural drop rule, and the quantities A_a and b_a are not defined precisely enough to establish the stated termination and violation guarantees. A specialized authoritative source is required.

children.title: Dual-Growth Methods
children.top_down_role: Families organized around coordinated evolution of dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Growth Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic primal-dual growth for nonnegative covering linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the covering program \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\), initialize \(y=0\) and an empty selected set \(S\). While some covering requirement is not represented as satisfied by \(S\), increase one or more corresponding coordinates of \(y\) continuously until a dual inequality \((A^\top y)_j\le c_j\) becomes tight; add such an index \(j\) to \(S\). Stop when \(S\) supports a primal-feasible solution, optionally prune \(S\), and output that solution together with \(y\). Approximation follows from a problem-specific charging inequality \(c^\top x\le\alpha b^\top y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grow feasible dual variables until constraints become tight, select the corresponding primal objects, then use dual value and charging to certify approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) are nonnegative.
Every unmet requirement has a positive coefficient in some finite-cost column.
The growth rule maintains dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c^\top x\le\alpha b^\top y\), then \(c^\top x\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited textbook section is relevant to primal-dual methods, but full-text support for this generic algorithm is pending. The displayed primal uses a continuous vector x, while the procedure operates on an undefined selected set S; 'represented as satisfied,' the growth rates, primal reconstruction, and pruning rule are problem-specific and not mathematically defined here.

children.title: Feasibility-Preserving Pruning

children.title: Reverse-Delete Postprocessing
children.top_down_role: Pruning organized by reversing the construction order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniqueness and order-independent cost quality for inclusion-minimal outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathcal F=\{S\subseteq E:S\ne\varnothing\}\), and \(c_a=1,c_b=M\) with \(M>1\). Starting from \(\{a,b\}\), testing \(a\) first returns \(\{b\}\) of cost \(M\), whereas testing \(b\) first returns \(\{a\}\) of cost \(1\). Hence reverse delete need not have a unique output or an order-independent approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different deletion orders can produce minimal feasible sets with arbitrarily different costs.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility means selecting at least one element.
knowledge_statements.title: Order Dependence of Reverse Delete

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural guarantee of a complete deletion scan over an upward-closed feasible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) be upward closed and let \(S_0\in\mathcal F\). Scan every element of \(S_0\) once in any fixed order, deleting it whenever the current set remains in \(\mathcal F\). The final set \(S_*\) satisfies \[S_*\in\mathcal F,\qquad S_*\setminus\{e\}\notin\mathcal F\quad\text{for every }e\in S_*.\] Thus \(S_*\) is inclusion-minimal in \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete reverse-delete scan of an upward-closed feasible family returns an inclusion-minimal feasible subset.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite.
\(\mathcal F\) is upward closed.
Every element of the initial feasible set is tested once.
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimality After Reverse Deletion
Reverse-Delete Postprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-order deletion from an upward-closed feasible covering solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite, let \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) be upward closed, and suppose a construction phase selected the ordered sequence \((e_1,\ldots,e_k)\) with \(S=\{e_1,\ldots,e_k\}\in\mathcal F\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), replace \(S\) by \(S\setminus\{e_i\}\) exactly when that set remains in \(\mathcal F\). Output the final set \(S'\). Then \(S'\in\mathcal F\); no element rejected by this reverse scan can be removed at its processing time; and, for nonnegative element costs, \(c(S')\le c(S)\). The method uses at most \(k\) feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan selected objects in reverse construction order and delete each object whose removal preserves feasibility; nonnegative cost cannot increase.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal F\) is upward closed.
The initial selected set is feasible.
Element costs are nonnegative for the cost conclusion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits Reverse-Delete Postprocessing, but the only locator is a general primal-dual-methods section and may not support the stated abstract reverse-delete procedure, its generic upward-closed setting, or its feasibility-test bound.

children.title: Redundancy Cleanup
children.top_down_role: Removal of primal structure that is unnecessary for the retained guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of a direct exhaustive implementation of redundant-element deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=|S|\), and suppose membership in \(\mathcal F\) is decided by an oracle. Scan the current set until a deletable element is found, restart after each successful deletion, and stop after a complete unsuccessful scan. There are at most \(n\) successful deletions and each scan tests at most \(n\) elements, so the procedure uses \(O(n^2)\) oracle calls. This excludes the internal cost of one membership test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct exhaustive redundancy cleanup uses quadratically many feasibility tests in the initial set size.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
Membership in \(\mathcal F\) is available through an oracle.

notation.meaning: Cardinality of the initial selected set.

knowledge_statements.title: Membership-Oracle Complexity of Repeated Cleanup

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inclusion Minimality Does Not Imply Minimum Cost or Confluence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of arbitrary-order redundancy deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{a,b,c\}\) and let \(\mathcal F\) be the upward-closed family generated by \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b,c\}\). Starting from \(E\), deleting \(a\) first yields the inclusion-minimal feasible set \(\{b,c\}\); deleting \(b\) first permits deletion of \(c\) and yields \(\{a\}\). With costs \(c_a=M\) and \(c_b=c_c=1\), where \(M>2\), the two outputs cost \(2\) and \(M\). Thus arbitrary-order cleanup is nonconfluent, need not minimize cost, and has no instance-independent approximation factor relative to the cheapest feasible subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different valid deletion orders can produce arbitrarily different inclusion-minimal feasible sets and costs.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is the upward closure of \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b,c\}\).

notation.meaning: Cost parameter producing an unbounded output ratio.

knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion Minimality Does Not Imply Minimum Cost or Confluence
Redundancy Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-independent deletion to an inclusion-minimal feasible subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite, \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) a feasible family, and \(S\in\mathcal F\). While there exists \(e\in S\) with \(S\setminus\{e\}\in\mathcal F\), delete any such \(e\). Output \(S^\star\) when no deletion applies. The procedure terminates after at most \(|S|\) successful deletions and satisfies
\[S^\star\in\mathcal F,\qquad S^\star\setminus\{e\}\notin\mathcal F\quad(e\in S^\star).\]
Thus the output is inclusion-minimal within the original set. If costs are additive and nonnegative, every deletion is nonincreasing in cost, so \(c(S^\star)\le c(S)\). Different deletion choices may produce different minimal subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete any individually redundant selected object until the feasible set is inclusion-minimal; with nonnegative costs, cleanup never increases cost.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite.
Membership in \(\mathcal F\) can be tested.
Costs are nonnegative for the cost conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^\star\) is feasible, inclusion-minimal, and satisfies \(c(S^\star)\le c(S)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cleanup algorithm is precise, terminates as claimed, and produces an inclusion-minimal feasible subset, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Feasibility-Preserving Pruning
children.top_down_role: Cleanup regimes classified by preserved feasibility requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate characterizing safe pruning of a selected covering solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite, let \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) be the feasible family, and let \(S\in\mathcal F\). A pruning operator \(\Pi: \mathcal F\to\mathcal F\) is feasibility preserving if
\[\Pi(S)\subseteq S\quad\text{and}\quad \Pi(S)\in\mathcal F\qquad(S\in\mathcal F).\]
It is inclusion-minimal if additionally
\[\Pi(S)\setminus\{e\}\notin\mathcal F\qquad(e\in\Pi(S)).\]
For an additive nonnegative cost function \(c(T)=\sum_{e\in T}c_e\), every feasibility-preserving pruning operator satisfies \(c(\Pi(S))\le c(S)\). Consequently pruning can remove redundant selected objects without invalidating feasibility or worsening a previously established upper cost bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe pruning returns a feasible subset of the selected objects; if it is minimal, no remaining object can be deleted, and nonnegative cost cannot increase.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite.
The initial set belongs to \(\mathcal F\).
Element costs are nonnegative for the cost conclusion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly characterizes feasibility-preserving pruning, and condition is a defensible role for this predicate-oriented leaf. However, no source supports the operator definition, minimality condition, or cost property.

children.title: Dual Fitting
children.top_down_role: Certificate construction through controlled adjustment of dual objects.

assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) are nonnegative.
\(x\) is primal feasible, \(y\ge 0\), and \(\alpha\ge 1\).
\(c^\top x\le b^\top y\) and \(A^\top y\le\alpha c\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of the displayed covering primal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation certificate obtained by scaling an infeasible dual construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the covering primal and packing dual
\[\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c,\ y\ge0\}.\]
Let \(\operatorname{OPT}\) denote the primal optimum. Suppose an algorithm returns a primal-feasible vector \(x\), a vector \(y\ge0\), and a scalar \(\alpha\ge1\) satisfying
\[c^\top x\le b^\top y\qquad\text{and}\qquad A^\top y\le\alpha c.\]
Then \(y/\alpha\) is dual feasible and
\[c^\top x\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}.\]
Thus \((x,y,\alpha)\) is a directly checkable dual-fitting certificate for an \(\alpha\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal solution, a nonnegative fitted dual vector, and a scaling factor certify an approximation when the scaled dual is feasible and its unscaled value covers the primal cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Fitting

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the covering primal and packing dual
\[\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c,\ y\ge0\},\]
let \(x\) and \(y\) be feasible, let \(\operatorname{OPT}\) denote the primal optimum, and let \(\alpha,\beta\ge1\). If
\[x_j>0\Rightarrow c_j\le\alpha(A^\top y)_j,\qquad y_i>0\Rightarrow (Ax)_i\le\beta b_i,\]
then
\[c^\top x\le\alpha\beta\operatorname{OPT}.\]
The feasible pair \((x,y)\) and the two support-wise inequalities constitute a directly checkable \(\alpha\beta\)-approximation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and dual solutions satisfying multiplicatively relaxed complementary-slackness inequalities certify an approximation factor equal to the product of the two relaxation factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Complementarity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.1 Interpretation of CS and the Dual Problem p. 162
source_witnesses.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive approximate-complementarity certificate for feasible covering and packing solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the covering primal and packing dual \[\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c,\ y\ge0\},\] every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\) satisfy \[c^\top x-b^\top y=\sum_jx_j\bigl(c_j-(A^\top y)_j\bigr)+\sum_i y_i\bigl((Ax)_i-b_i\bigr).\] Both sums are nonnegative. If their total is at most \(\varepsilon\), then \(x\) is additively \(\varepsilon\)-optimal; total zero is complementary slackness and certifies optimality of both solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual gap equals the sum of variable-weighted dual slacks and dual-variable-weighted primal surpluses.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is primal feasible.
\(y\) is dual feasible.

children.title: Lagrangian-Relaxation Methods
children.top_down_role: Approximation families based on penalized tractable subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
The complicating constraints are \(Ax\ge b\).
The inner optimization over \(X\) is well-defined for every multiplier considered by the method.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the original constrained minimization problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method based on solving penalized tractable subproblems and updating nonnegative multipliers.

source_refs.source_title: A First Course in Combinatorial Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[z^*=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\},\]
where optimization over \(X\) is tractable and \(Ax\ge b\) is the family of complicating constraints. For each multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\), define
\[L(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\bigl(c^\top x+\lambda^\top(b-Ax)\bigr),\qquad z_{LD}=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}L(\lambda).\]
A Lagrangian-relaxation method selects or updates multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\), solves the corresponding inner problem defining \(L(\lambda)\), and records the resulting lower bounds. For every considered multiplier,
\[L(\lambda)\le z_{LD}\le z^*.\]
Any construction of a feasible solution of the original problem requires a separately specified primal-recovery rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian-relaxation method moves complicating constraints into the objective with nonnegative multipliers, solves the resulting tractable subproblems, and updates the multipliers while retaining valid lower bounds; primal recovery is problem-specific.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian-Relaxation Methods

source_witnesses.source_title: A First Course in Combinatorial Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality test using a feasible relaxed minimizer and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_\lambda\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(b-Ax)\}\). If \(Ax_\lambda\ge b\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda^\top(Ax_\lambda-b)=0\), then \(L(\lambda)=c^\top x_\lambda=z^*\). Thus \(x_\lambda\) is optimal for the original minimization problem and \(\lambda\) attains the Lagrangian-dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible relaxed minimizer satisfying complementary slackness certifies zero Lagrangian gap and global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The original minimization problem is feasible.
The relaxed minimum is attained by \(x_\lambda\).
\(Ax_\lambda\ge b\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda^\top(Ax_\lambda-b)=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Lagrangian Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonic Tradeoff of Exact Scalar-Penalty Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric behavior of exact penalized minimizers under a scalar multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_i\in\arg\min_S\{c(S)+\lambda_i p(S)\}\) for \(0\le\lambda_1<\lambda_2\), with both minima attained. Then \(p(S_2)\le p(S_1)\) and \(c(S_1)\le c(S_2)\). Nonunique minimizers may make either inequality an equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing a scalar penalty multiplier weakly decreases the penalty and weakly increases structural cost among exact selected optima.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\lambda_1<\lambda_2\).
Both penalized minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonic Tradeoff of Exact Scalar-Penalty Optima

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concavity and Supergradients of the Lagrangian Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric structure supporting multiplier-update methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(b-Ax)\}\), \(L\) is concave on its finite-valued domain in \(\mathbb R_+^m\). If \(x_\lambda\) attains the infimum, then \(g_\lambda=b-Ax_\lambda\) is a supergradient: \(L(\mu)\le L(\lambda)+g_\lambda^\top(\mu-\lambda)\) for every \(\mu\ge0\) at which \(L(\mu)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian value is concave, and a relaxed minimizer's constraint residual is a supergradient for multiplier updates.
assumptions_latex: The displayed Lagrangian values are finite.
\(x_\lambda\) attains the relaxed infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Concavity and Supergradients of the Lagrangian Value

children.title: Lagrangian-Multiplier-Preserving Methods
children.top_down_role: Families preserving approximation behavior across penalty parameters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate approximation consequence of the multiplier-preserving inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(c(S),p(S)\ge0\), \(\alpha\ge1\), and for every \(\lambda\ge0\) an algorithm returns \(S_\lambda\) satisfying \(c(S_\lambda)+\alpha\lambda p(S_\lambda)\le\alpha\min_S\{c(S)+\lambda p(S)\}\). At \(\lambda=1\), it follows that \(c(S_1)+p(S_1)\le\alpha\min_S\{c(S)+p(S)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every alpha-LMP algorithm is an alpha-approximation for the unscaled prize-collecting objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\ge1\).
The LMP inequality holds at \(\lambda=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: LMP Guarantee Implies Prize-Collecting Approximation
Lagrangian-Multiplier-Preserving Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard multiplier-preserving guarantee for prize-collecting minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(S)\ge 0\) be the structural cost of a feasible object \(S\), and let \(p(S)\ge 0\) be its uncovered-demand penalty. For every multiplier \(\lambda\ge 0\), define \(\operatorname{OPT}(\lambda)=\min_S\{c(S)+\lambda p(S)\}\). An algorithm is \(\alpha\)-Lagrangian-multiplier-preserving if its output \(S_\lambda\) satisfies \[c(S_\lambda)+\alpha\lambda p(S_\lambda)\le \alpha\operatorname{OPT}(\lambda)\] for every \(\lambda\ge0\). Equivalently, the structural cost is charged once while the penalty remains scaled by the same approximation factor under every multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alpha-LMP algorithm preserves its approximation guarantee uniformly across penalty multipliers, with the penalty multiplied by alpha on the algorithmic side.
assumptions_latex: \(c(S),p(S)\ge0\) for every feasible \(S\).
\(\lambda\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Optimal Lagrangian objective at multiplier lambda.

children.title: Hyperplane Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected approximation ratio for nonnegative weighted Max-Cut objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{-1\le t<1}\frac{2\arccos(t)}{\pi(1-t)}\approx0.87856.\] For unit vectors \(v_i\) and nonnegative edge weights \(w_{ij}\), random-hyperplane rounding satisfies \[\mathbb E[w(\delta(S))]=\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\frac{\arccos(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)}{\pi}\ge \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\frac{1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle}{2}.\] Hence rounding an optimal Max-Cut SDP solution has expected value at least \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{cut}}\). Nonnegative weights are required for the termwise comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Angular separation dominates the SDP edge contribution by the Goemans–Williamson constant, giving an expected Max-Cut ratio of about 0.87856.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ij}\ge0\) for every edge.

notation.meaning: Minimum ratio of angular separation probability to the SDP edge contribution.
One side of the rounded cut.
