knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Semidefinite Relaxation for Minimum Bisection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-specific nondegenerate vector relaxation preserving exact balance in its integral embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For even \(n\), assign each vertex a unit vector \(v_u\), impose \(\sum_{u\in V}v_u=0\), and minimize \(\frac14\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv}\|v_u-v_v\|^2\). Every exact bisection embeds by choosing a unit vector \(a\), setting \(v_u=a\) on one side and \(v_u=-a\) on the other. The objective then equals the cut weight, so \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{bis}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit vectors with zero total vector give a semidefinite lower bound whose integral embeddings are exact bisections.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected with nonnegative edge weights.
The number of vertices is even.

notation.meaning: Optimum of the balanced vector relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Semidefinite Relaxation for Minimum Bisection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Dynamic Programming on Tree Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially solvable restricted regime for weighted exact minimum bisection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Root a weighted tree \(T\). For every rooted subtree \(T_v\), cardinality \(q\), and bit \(b\), store the minimum weight of cut edges internal to \(T_v\) among assignments placing exactly \(q\) vertices of \(T_v\) on the designated side and placing \(v\) on side \(b\). Knapsack convolution over the children, charging \(vu\) exactly when its endpoint bits differ, computes an exact balanced cut in polynomial time. At the root select the cardinality prescribed by the even- or odd-order convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree-cardinality dynamic program solves weighted minimum bisection exactly on trees.
assumptions_latex: The input graph is a finite weighted tree.
Edge weights are nonnegative.
The required side cardinality is fixed by the chosen balance convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{bis}}(T)\text{ is computable exactly in polynomial time}.

notation.meaning: Number of subtree vertices on the designated side.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Dynamic Programming on Tree Instances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility and optimality test for zero cut cost under nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be even and let \(H=(V,\{uv\in E:w_{uv}>0\})\), with connected components \(C_1,\ldots,C_t\). A bisection \(S\) has cost zero if and only if \(S\) is a union of components of \(H\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{bis}}=0\) exactly when some subcollection of the component sizes sums to \(n/2\); the corresponding union certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-cost bisection exists exactly when the positive-weight components can be divided into two equal-size vertex groups.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected.
Edge weights are nonnegative.
The number of vertices is even.

notation.meaning: Subgraph containing exactly the positive-weight edges.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact balanced-cut objective for undirected graphs with even order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with nonnegative edge weights and even \(n=|V|\). A bisection is a set \(S\subset V\) satisfying \(|S|=n/2\). Its cost is the total weight of edges with exactly one endpoint in \(S\). The minimum-bisection problem is \[\min_{S\subset V:\,|S|=n/2}\ \sum_{uv\in E:\,u\in S,\,v\notin S}w_{uv}.\] For odd \(n\), the balanced convention replaces equality by \(\bigl||S|-|V\setminus S|\bigr|\le 1\).

children.title: Linear Arrangement Frontier
children.top_down_role: Approximation behavior for ordering vertices under edge-length costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-complexity boundary for the unweighted problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing a minimum-cost linear arrangement is NP-hard even for unweighted undirected graphs. Thus, unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), no polynomial-time algorithm always returns an optimal arrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum linear arrangement is NP-hard even on unweighted undirected graphs.
assumptions_latex: Hardness uses the standard explicit graph representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}\Rightarrow\text{no polynomial-time exact algorithm for all instances}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical ordering objective; the seed supplies its cut-sum equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with nonnegative weights, a linear arrangement is a bijection \(\pi:V\to\{1,\ldots,|V|\}\). Its cost is \(\operatorname{LA}(\pi)=\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|\), and minimum linear arrangement minimizes this cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum linear arrangement orders vertices to minimize total weighted edge length along a line.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and undirected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary lower-bound certificate derived from the prefix-cut representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(G\) is a connected unweighted graph on \(n\) vertices, every nontrivial prefix \(S_i\) of any arrangement satisfies \(|\delta(S_i)|\ge1\). Hence \(\operatorname{LA}(\pi)=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|\delta(S_i)|\ge n-1\). Equality holds exactly when every prefix cut has one crossing edge, which occurs precisely when \(G\) is a path and \(\pi\) lists its vertices in a path order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity certifies the lower bound n−1, attained exactly by arranging a path in path order.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, connected, simple, and unweighted.
\(\pi\) is a vertex bijection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LA}(\pi)\ge n-1,\qquad \operatorname{LA}(\pi)=n-1\iff G\text{ is a path ordered along that path}.

notation.meaning: Prefix of size i in the arrangement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spreading-relaxation approximation regime for general minimum linear arrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for \(n\)-vertex minimum linear arrangement with expected approximation factor \(O(\sqrt{\log n}\,\log\log n)\), based on a spreading relaxation followed by multiscale decomposition and ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General minimum linear arrangement admits a polylogarithmic approximation based on spreading relaxations and decomposition.
assumptions_latex: The graph is explicitly represented.
The precise weighted-versus-unweighted scope must follow the cited theorem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical restricted unweighted graph class for minimum linear arrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimum linear arrangement on an unweighted tree is solvable exactly in polynomial time: given a tree \(T\), an algorithm returns a bijection \(\pi\) minimizing \(\sum_{uv\in E(T)}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Although minimum linear arrangement is NP-hard on general graphs, it is exactly polynomial-time solvable on unweighted trees.
assumptions_latex: The input graph is an explicitly represented unweighted tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MinLA}(T)\text{ is computable exactly in polynomial time}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Subset Dynamic Program for Minimum Linear Arrangement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exponential-time algorithm derived from the prefix-cut identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(U)=w(\delta(U))\), define \(F(\varnothing)=0\), and for nonempty \(U\subseteq V\) define \[F(U)=c(U)+\min_{v\in U}F(U\setminus\{v\}).\] Since \(c(V)=0\), \(F(V)=\operatorname{OPT}_{LA}\). Recording a minimizing vertex at each state recovers an optimal ordering. After all cut weights are available, the recurrence uses \(O(n2^n)\) time and \(O(2^n)\) stored values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset dynamic program exactly minimizes the sum of prefix-cut weights by selecting the last vertex of each prefix set.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected.
Edge weights are nonnegative and represented exactly.

notation.meaning: Minimum accumulated cut-sum for arranging the vertices of U before its complement.
Weight of the cut between U and its complement in V.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) have connected components \(G_1,\ldots,G_t\) and nonnegative edge weights. There exists an optimal arrangement in which each component occupies a contiguous block, and \[\operatorname{OPT}_{LA}(G)=\sum_{r=1}^t\operatorname{OPT}_{LA}(G_r).\]

Linear Arrangement Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-sum representation of the weighted minimum linear arrangement objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with nonnegative weights and \(n=|V|\). For a bijection \(\pi:V\to\{1,\ldots,n\}\), put \(S_i=\{v:\pi(v)\le i\}\). Then the weighted linear-arrangement cost has the exact representation \[\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}w(\delta(S_i)).\] Hence minimum linear arrangement is equivalently the problem of choosing a nested sequence \(S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_{n-1}\), with \(|S_i|=i\), minimizing the sum of its cut weights.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spreading Feasibility Is Not Line-Metric Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explains why the spreading system is a relaxation rather than an integral description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible region of spreading semimetrics is strictly broader than the set of metrics \(d_\pi(u,v)=|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|\) induced by injective line placements. Consequently, a feasible spreading semimetric does not by itself specify an arrangement; an additional embedding or rounding theorem is required to obtain one with a controlled objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible spreading semimetric need not be a line metric, so a separate rounding theorem is required.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation permits arbitrary real semimetrics satisfying the spreading inequalities.
review_flags: An explicit strict-containment witness or authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spreading-Semimetric Relaxation for Minimum Linear Arrangement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical relaxation connection to the sibling arrangement objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv}d(u,v)\) over semimetrics satisfying \(\sum_{v\in S}d(u,v)\ge\lfloor|S|^2/4\rfloor\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\) and \(u\in S\). Every arrangement line metric \(d_\pi(u,v)=|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|\) is feasible and has objective equal to its arrangement cost; hence \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{spread}}\le\operatorname{OPT}_{LA}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing edge length over spreading semimetrics relaxes minimum linear arrangement and gives a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and nonnegatively weighted.
\(d\) is symmetric, nonnegative, zero on the diagonal, and satisfies triangle inequalities.
review_flags: The normalization inherits the immutable seed's unresolved source requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Separation of Arrangement Spreading Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation for the seed-normalized subset inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(u\in V\), sort \(V\setminus\{u\}\) by nondecreasing \(d(u,v)\). For each cardinality \(s\), the minimum of \(\sum_{v\in S}d(u,v)\) over \(S\ni u\), \(|S|=s\), is attained by \(u\) and its \(s-1\) nearest vertices. Checking all such prefixes separates every inequality \(\sum_{v\in S}d(u,v)\ge\lfloor s^2/4\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorting distances from each center and checking every nearest-neighbor prefix separates all spreading inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
The seed normalization \(\lfloor |S|^2/4\rfloor\) is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Separation of Arrangement Spreading Constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equilateral Spreading Metric Outside the Line-Metric Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit strict-containment witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|V|=n\ge3\), set \(d(u,u)=0\), and set \(d(u,v)=c_n:=\max_{2\le s\le n}\lfloor s^2/4\rfloor/(s-1)\) for \(u\ne v\). Then \((s-1)c_n\ge\lfloor s^2/4\rfloor\), so every spreading inequality holds. No injective line placement of three or more points has all positive pairwise distances equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitably scaled equilateral metric is spreading-feasible but is not an arrangement line metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\in P_{\mathrm{spread}}\quad\text{and}\quad d\ne d_\pi\text{ for every injective line placement }\pi.

notation.meaning: equilateral scaling satisfying every cardinality bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Optimization of the Finite Spreading Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity consequence of exact separation for the seed-normalized relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational input data, the spreading-semimetric linear relaxation with symmetry, diagonal, nonnegativity, triangle, and spreading constraints can be optimized in polynomial time by the ellipsoid method using the nearest-neighbor-prefix separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial-time separation makes the rational spreading-semimetric LP polynomial-time optimizable.
assumptions_latex: The finite instance and coefficients are rational and binary encoded.
The seed-normalized spreading inequalities and standard semimetric constraints are used.
The relaxation is feasible and has a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radius Growth Forced by Spreading Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequence of the seed-normalized arrangement spreading inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a semimetric satisfies \(\sum_{v\in S}d(u,v)\ge\lfloor |S|^2/4\rfloor\), then every set \(S\ni u\) of size \(s\ge2\) contains a vertex \(v\) with \[d(u,v)\ge\frac{\lfloor s^2/4\rfloor}{s-1}.\] Equivalently, a ball centered at \(u\) with radius smaller than this quantity contains fewer than \(s\) vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spreading inequalities prevent too many vertices from lying in a small-radius semimetric ball.
assumptions_latex: The seed-normalized spreading inequalities hold for every nonempty subset and every center in that subset.
knowledge_statements.title: Radius Growth Forced by Spreading Constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite LP Dual of the Spreading-Semimetric Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound certificate for a fixed finite encoding of the arrangement spreading LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index unordered vertex pairs by \(P\). Let \(Ad\ge b\) encode the spreading inequalities, where row \((u,S)\) has coefficient one on \(\{u,v\}\) for \(v\in S\setminus\{u\}\) and \(b_{u,S}=\lfloor|S|^2/4\rfloor\). Let \(Td\ge0\) encode \(d_{uw}+d_{wv}-d_{uv}\ge0\), and let \(c_{uv}=w_{uv}\) on graph edges and zero otherwise. The dual of \(\min\{c^Td:Ad\ge b,\ Td\ge0,\ d\ge0\}\) is \[\max\ b^T\alpha\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A^T\alpha+T^T\gamma\le c,\qquad \alpha,\gamma\ge0.\] Every feasible \((\alpha,\gamma)\) certifies the lower bound \(b^T\alpha\), and strong duality gives equality when the finite primal is feasible and bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative prices on spreading and triangle inequalities form the dual certificate for the finite spreading LP.
assumptions_latex: The vertex set is finite.
Weights and the fixed LP encoding are rational.
The primal spreading LP is feasible and has finite optimum.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative dual prices for spreading and triangle inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(d:V\times V\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) be a semimetric. The arrangement spreading condition requires that, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\) and every \(u\in S\), \[\sum_{v\in S}d(u,v)\ge \left\lfloor\frac{|S|^2}{4}\right\rfloor.\] Every integral line metric \(d_\pi(u,v)=|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|\), induced by an injective placement \(\pi:V\to\mathbb{Z}\), satisfies these inequalities. Thus the condition is a valid relaxation of the dispersion forced by a linear arrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spreading constraints require every subset to remain sufficiently dispersed around each member; all metrics induced by injective integer arrangements satisfy them.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic Lower Bound for Oblivious Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case optimality boundary for undirected demand-independent fractional routing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are families of \(n\)-vertex undirected capacitated graphs for which every oblivious fractional routing scheme has competitive ratio \(\Omega(\log n)\). Together with the logarithmic tree-based upper bound, the worst-case undirected frontier is \(\Theta(\log n)\) under the same congestion convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some undirected graphs force logarithmic competitive ratio, making the logarithmic oblivious-routing guarantee asymptotically optimal.
assumptions_latex: Routing is demand-independent and fractional.
Performance is compared with demand-aware optimal congestion.
Upper and lower bounds use the same load and expectation convention.
review_flags: authoritative_source_required: undirected oblivious-routing lower bound under the stated model
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic Lower Bound for Oblivious Routing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier convention for distributions over routing operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a randomized oblivious scheme samples a routing operator \(R\) independently of \(D\), its expected-load competitive guarantee is \[\sup_{D\ne0}\frac{\max_{e\in E}\mathbb E_R[\operatorname{load}_e(R,D)/c_e]}{\rho_G(D)}.\] This differs from \(\sup_D\mathbb E_R[\max_e\operatorname{load}_e(R,D)/c_e]/\rho_G(D)\); the latter is stronger and must not be inferred without an additional concentration or deterministic-mixture argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum expected edge load and expected maximum congestion are distinct conventions for randomized oblivious routing.
assumptions_latex: The routing operator is sampled independently of the demand matrix.
Edge capacities are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_e\mathbb E_R[L_e]\le\mathbb E_R[\max_eL_e],\text{ and the two guarantees are not interchangeable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized-Scheme Expectation Convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oblivious Fractional Routing and Competitive Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demand-independent fractional routing and its worst-case congestion measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An oblivious fractional routing scheme fixes, for every ordered pair \((s,t)\), a unit \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow \(R_{st}\) before the demand matrix \(D\) is known. It routes \(D\) as \(\sum_{s,t}D_{st}R_{st}\). Its competitive ratio is \[\operatorname{comp}(R)=\sup_{D\ne0}\frac{\rho_R(D)}{\rho_G(D)},\] where \(\rho_R(D)\) is the resulting maximum capacity-normalized edge load and \(\rho_G(D)\) is the minimum congestion of a demand-aware fractional routing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oblivious routing fixes pairwise flows before demands are known and compares their worst-case congestion with demand-aware optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and positively capacitated.
Demands are nonnegative and fractional routing is allowed.
The comparison excludes the zero demand matrix.

notation.meaning: fixed unit flow for ordered pair (s,t)
congestion induced by the oblivious scheme

knowledge_statements.title: Oblivious Fractional Routing and Competitive Ratio
Oblivious Routing Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demand-independent routing in capacitated undirected graphs via probabilistic tree embeddings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E,c)\) be an undirected graph with positive capacities. There exists a polynomial-time constructible randomized oblivious routing scheme that fixes, before demands are known, a distribution of routes for every ordered vertex pair. For every feasible nonnegative demand matrix \(D\), if \(\rho_G(D)\) is the minimum possible congestion of a demand-aware routing and \(\rho_{\mathcal R}(D)\) is the expected congestion under the fixed scheme, then \[\rho_{\mathcal R}(D)\le O(\log |V|)\rho_G(D).\] The scheme may be represented through a distribution over capacity-dominating routing trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undirected graphs admit polynomial-time demand-independent routing schemes whose expected congestion is within O(log n) of demand-aware optimal congestion.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and has positive capacities.
Demands are nonnegative and simultaneously routable fractionally.
Congestion is measured relative to edge capacity.

notation.meaning: expected congestion of the oblivious scheme

For \(S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_k\}\), \(\max_{x\in X}d(x,S)\le2\operatorname{OPT}\). Maintaining nearest-center distances uses \(O(k|X|)\) distance evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly selecting a point farthest from the current centers gives a factor-two metric k-center solution.

Every point is an eligible center.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\ge0\), let \(G_r\) have vertex set \(X\) and edge \(xy\) whenever \(d(x,y)\le r\). A set \(S\subseteq X\) with \(|S|\le k\) has radius at most \(r\) if and only if its closed neighborhoods cover \(X\), equivalently, \(S\) is a dominating set of size at most \(k\) in \(G_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius-r k-center feasibility is exactly domination by at most k vertices in the distance-threshold graph.
assumptions_latex: Centers and clients are both \(X\).

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a finite metric space.
Every point is both a client and an eligible center.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp polynomial-time approximation threshold for standard metric k-center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite metric space \((X,d)\) and an integer \(1\le k\le |X|\), metric \(k\)-center minimizes \(\max_{x\in X}d(x,S)\) over sets \(S\subseteq X\) with \(|S|\le k\), where \(d(x,S)=\min_{s\in S}d(x,s)\). A polynomial-time algorithm returns a set \(S\) with radius at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}\). Moreover, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), a polynomial-time \((2-\varepsilon)\)-approximation would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical uncapacitated discrete-facility formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite client and facility sets \(C,F\) in a metric \((X,d)\) and \(1\le k\le|F|\), metric \(k\)-median chooses \(S\subseteq F\), \(|S|\le k\), minimizing \(\sum_{j\in C}d(j,S)\), where \(d(j,S)=\min_{i\in S}d(j,i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric k-median opens at most k facilities and minimizes total nearest-facility distance.

\(d\) is a metric.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Link to Uniform-Cost Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact penalization relation explaining the facility-location connection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Removing \(\sum_i y_i\le k\) and adding multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\) gives objective \(\sum_{i,j}d(i,j)x_{ij}+\lambda\sum_i y_i-\lambda k\). Apart from \(-\lambda k\), this is the facility-location relaxation with uniform opening cost \(\lambda\). Its minimum \(L(\lambda)\) is a lower bound on the constrained k-median LP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalizing the facility-count constraint turns the relaxation into uniform-cost facility location and yields a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda\ge0\).
The relaxed cardinality constraint is \(\sum_i y_i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Link to Uniform-Cost Facility Location

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard relaxation supporting rounding and Lagrangian methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical relaxation minimizes \(\sum_{i\in F,j\in C}d(i,j)x_{ij}\) subject to \(\sum_i x_{ij}=1\) for each \(j\), \(0\le x_{ij}\le y_i\), \(0\le y_i\le1\), and \(\sum_i y_i\le k\). Integral feasible solutions encode at most \(k\) open facilities and complete client assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard k-median LP fractionally opens at most k facilities and assigns each client to opened mass.
assumptions_latex: The metric k-median instance is finite.

notation.meaning: fraction of client j assigned to facility i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Certificate for an Equivalent Standard k-Median LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual of the accepted assignment-opening relaxation after omitting individually redundant opening upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because any feasible opening vector may be capped coordinatewise at one without harming assignment feasibility or increasing cost, the accepted relaxation is equivalent in value to the formulation with \(y_i\ge0\), \(x_{ij}\le y_i\), and \(\sum_i y_i\le k\), omitting explicit constraints \(y_i\le1\). A dual of this equivalent formulation is \[\max\ \sum_{j\in C}\alpha_j-k\lambda\] subject to \(\alpha_j\le d(i,j)+\beta_{ij}\) for all \(i,j\), \(\sum_j\beta_{ij}\le\lambda\) for every \(i\), and \(\beta_{ij},\lambda\ge0\), with \(\alpha_j\) unrestricted. Every feasible \((\alpha,\beta,
\lambda)\) lower-bounds the integral optimum; equality with a feasible primal solution certifies LP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After removing redundant opening upper bounds, client values, linkage contributions, and a cardinality price form the standard k-median LP dual certificate.
assumptions_latex: The instance is finite.
The primal uses \(\sum_i y_i\le k\) and nonnegative assignment costs.

notation.meaning: Dual price of the facility-count bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The comparison inequalities establishing the \((3+2/p)\) p-swap bound use the triangle inequality to reroute clients through local and comparator facilities. For an integer \(p\ge1\), call \(S\subseteq F\), \(|S|=k\), a \(p\)-swap local optimum if replacing at most \(p\) centers of \(S\) by the same number of facilities never decreases \(\sum_{x\in C}d(x,S)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical opening-plus-connection objective, distinct from fixed-cardinality k-median.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite facilities \(F\), clients \(C\), opening costs \(f_i\ge0\), and metric connection costs \(c_{ij}\), uncapacitated facility location chooses a nonempty \(S\subseteq F\) minimizing \(\sum_{i\in S}f_i+\sum_{j\in C}\min_{i\in S}c_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric uncapacitated facility location trades facility-opening costs against client connection costs.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(C\) are finite.
Connection costs are restrictions of a common metric.
At least one facility is eligible.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Uncapacitated Facility Location

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates ordinary UFL guarantees from hard-capacitated and bicriteria variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After imposing \(\sum_j d_jx_{ij}\le u_i y_i\), an uncapacitated-facility-location approximation theorem no longer applies automatically. An algorithm that exceeds capacities or opens extra facility copies gives a bicriteria or resource-augmented guarantee unless the target formulation explicitly permits that behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard capacities change the approximation regime; capacity violation or extra copies must be reported as resource augmentation.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i\) is a hard capacity and \(d_j\) is client demand.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Sensitive Regime Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical metric uncapacitated facility-location regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Raise client dual values until connection constraints or facility budgets become tight, tentatively open funded facilities, and prune conflicting tentative facilities so every client connects to a surviving facility. For metric uncapacitated facility location, the classical growth-and-pruning construction returns a feasible solution of cost at most \(3\sum_j\alpha_j\le3\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical dual growth followed by pruning gives a factor-three approximation for metric uncapacitated facility location.
assumptions_latex: Connection costs form a metric.
Facilities are uncapacitated.
Opening costs are nonnegative.
The client values are feasible for the standard UFL dual.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Growth-and-Pruning Primal-Dual Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical local-search frontier for metric uncapacitated facility location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a feasible facility set, repeatedly perform an improving move that opens one facility, closes one facility, or swaps one open and one closed facility, reassigning clients to nearest open facilities. With a standard polynomial improvement threshold, this yields a polynomial-time \((3+\varepsilon)\)-approximation for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholded add-delete-swap local search gives a 3+epsilon approximation for metric UFL.
assumptions_latex: Connection costs form a metric.
Facilities are uncapacitated.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is fixed.
A polynomial improvement threshold is enforced.

notation.meaning: Approximation slack used for polynomial termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Add-Delete-Swap Local-Search Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard-Capacity Feasibility Failure of an Uncapacitated Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete colocated-demand witness that an uncapacitated guarantee does not transfer to hard capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two unit-demand clients and two facility labels \(p,q\) at one location, so all connection costs are zero. Let \(f_p=0\), \(f_q=M>0\), and impose hard capacities \(u_p=u_q=1\), with at most one copy of each facility. The uncapacitated optimum opens only \(p\) at cost zero and serves both clients, but that solution violates \(p\)'s capacity. Every feasible hard-capacitated solution opens both facilities and costs \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-cost uncapacitated solution can be infeasible under hard capacities, while every feasible capacitated solution has arbitrarily large opening cost.
assumptions_latex: There are two unit-demand clients colocated with the two facility labels.
At most one copy of each facility may be opened.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Capacity Feasibility Failure of an Uncapacitated Solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical greedy approximation regime for metric uncapacitated facility location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Metric uncapacitated facility location admits a polynomial-time greedy dual-fitting algorithm that grows client prices, opens facilities at specified tight events, and connects or reassigns clients according to the resulting tight structure, returning a feasible solution of cost at most \(1.61\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{UFL}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical greedy dual-fitting algorithm gives a 1.61-approximation for metric uncapacitated facility location.
assumptions_latex: Connection costs form a metric.
Facilities are uncapacitated.
Opening costs are nonnegative.
The event ordering and reassignment rule are those of the corresponding greedy dual-fitting theorem.

notation.meaning: Returned facility set with its induced client assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Dual-Fitting Approximation Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set Cover Embedding in Nonmetric Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-preserving reduction showing why metricity is essential to constant-factor UFL guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a set-cover instance with universe \(U\), covering family \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), and \(M=m+1\), create facility \(i\) with opening cost one and a client for each \(u\in U\). Set \(c_{iu}=0\) when \(u\in S_i\) and \(c_{iu}=M\) otherwise. The resulting uncapacitated nonmetric facility-location instance satisfies \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{UFL}}=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{SetCover}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary nonmetric facility location contains set cover through a cost-preserving reduction.
assumptions_latex: The set family covers \(U\).
Connection costs need not satisfy the triangle inequality.
Facilities are uncapacitated.

notation.meaning: Penalty for assigning an element to a set that does not contain it.

knowledge_statements.title: Set Cover Embedding in Nonmetric Facility Location
Facility-Location Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard LP duality underlying uncapacitated metric facility-location algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clients \(C\), facilities \(F\), opening costs \(f_i\ge0\), and metric connection costs \(c_{ij}\), the standard relaxation is \[\min\ \sum_{i\in F}f_i y_i+\sum_{i\in F,j\in C}c_{ij}x_{ij}\] subject to \(\sum_i x_{ij}=1\), \(0\le x_{ij}\le y_i\), and \(y_i\ge0\). Its dual is \[\max\ \sum_{j\in C}\alpha_j\] subject to \(\alpha_j\le c_{ij}+\beta_{ij}\), \(\sum_{j\in C}\beta_{ij}\le f_i\), and \(\alpha_j,\beta_{ij}\ge0\). For finite instances, strong linear-programming duality makes the two optimum values equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The facility-location LP balances opening and assignment costs; its dual allocates client contributions subject to each facility’s opening-cost budget.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(F\) are finite.
Opening and connection costs are nonnegative.
The primal relaxation is feasible.

notation.meaning: fractional opening variable for facility i
fraction of client j assigned to facility i

review_flags: A facility-location-specific source for the primal-dual formulation is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-dual pair is plausible and duality is an appropriate content kind for the facility-location container. A facility-location-specific source is required, particularly because the equality constraint ordinarily yields an unrestricted dual client variable before a nonnegativity normalization is justified.

children.title: Correlation-Clustering Frontier
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial and semidefinite approaches to agreement and disagreement objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical combinatorial approximation for unweighted minimum disagreement on complete signed graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly choose a uniformly random remaining pivot \(v\), output the cluster containing \(v\) and all its remaining positive neighbors, and delete that cluster. On an unweighted complete signed graph, the resulting partition satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[D(\Pi)]\le3\operatorname{OPT}_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random pivot is an expected factor-three approximation for complete unweighted minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
assumptions_latex: The signed graph is complete and unweighted.
Each pivot is uniform among the remaining vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Pivot Three-Approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PTAS Regime for Complete-Graph Maximum Agreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete unweighted maximum-agreement regime; the seed explains why it does not transfer multiplicatively to minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), maximum-agreement correlation clustering on complete unweighted signed graphs admits a polynomial-time algorithm producing \(\Pi\) with \(A(\Pi)\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_A\); the polynomial's exponent may depend on \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete unweighted maximum agreement has a PTAS, but this does not yield a minimum-disagreement PTAS.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\) is fixed.
The signed graph is complete and unweighted.
review_flags: A direct theorem locator is required for the PTAS and its running-time regime.
knowledge_statements.title: PTAS Regime for Complete-Graph Maximum Agreement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical unweighted complete signed-graph formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a complete graph whose edges are labeled \(+\) or \(-\), a partition \(\Pi\) incurs one disagreement for each positive edge crossing clusters and each negative edge within a cluster. Minimum disagreement minimizes this number; maximum agreement maximizes the complementary number of correctly classified edges. The number of clusters is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlation clustering partitions a complete signed graph without fixing the number of clusters, minimizing inconsistent edges or maximizing consistent edges.
assumptions_latex: The graph is complete and every edge has exactly one sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Graph Correlation-Clustering Objectives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical relaxation and lower-bound certificate for complete weighted correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each unordered pair \(\{u,v\}\), let \(x_{uv}\in[0,1]\) denote fractional separation and impose \(x_{uv}\le x_{uw}+x_{wv}\) for all distinct \(u,v,w\). Minimize \[\sum_{uv\in E^+}w_{uv}x_{uv}+\sum_{uv\in E^-}w_{uv}(1-x_{uv}).\] Every partition embeds by setting \(x_{uv}=1\) exactly when \(u\) and \(v\) lie in different clusters, so the LP optimum lower-bounds minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The triangle-inequality semimetric LP fractionally represents cluster separation and lower-bounds minimum disagreement.
assumptions_latex: The signed graph is complete.
Pair weights are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Fractional separation of vertices u and v.

knowledge_statements.title: Semimetric LP for Minimum Disagreement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Near-Optimal Agreement with No Finite Disagreement Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete witness for failure of multiplicative transfer from maximum agreement to minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_n\) have every edge labeled positive. The one-cluster partition has \(D^*=0\) and \(A^*=\binom n2\). The partition consisting of one singleton and one cluster of size \(n-1\) has \(D=n-1\) and \(A=\binom n2-(n-1)=(1-2/n)A^*\). Thus its agreement ratio tends to one, while no finite multiplicative disagreement guarantee is possible because its disagreement is positive and \(D^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an all-positive complete graph, isolating one vertex is nearly optimal for agreement but admits no finite multiplicative disagreement ratio.
assumptions_latex: The graph is complete, unweighted, and all edges are positive.

notation.meaning: Agreement and disagreement counts of the displayed partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Optimal Agreement with No Finite Disagreement Ratio

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial lower bound for complete unweighted minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inconsistent triangle has two positive edges and one negative edge, and every partition disagrees with at least one of its edges. If nonnegative values \(\lambda_T\) are assigned to inconsistent triangles with \(\sum_{T\ni e}\lambda_T\le1\) for every edge \(e\), then \(\sum_T\lambda_T\le\operatorname{OPT}_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional packing of inconsistent signed triangles is a verifiable lower bound on minimum disagreement.
assumptions_latex: The signed graph is complete and unweighted.
Every packed triangle has exactly two positive edges and one negative edge.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative packing weight of inconsistent triangle T.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent-Triangle Packing Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted complete signed graphs under the minimum-disagreement objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each edge \(e\) have weight \(w_e\ge0\). For every triangle \(T\) having exactly two positive edges and one negative edge, choose \(\lambda_T\ge0\) subject to \(\sum_{T\ni e}\lambda_T\le w_e\) for every edge \(e\). Then \(\sum_T\lambda_T\le\operatorname{OPT}_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional packing of inconsistent triangles into weighted edge capacities lower-bounds weighted minimum disagreement.
assumptions_latex: The signed graph is complete.
All edge weights are nonnegative.
Every indexed triangle has exactly two positive edges and one negative edge.

notation.meaning: Packing weight assigned to inconsistent triangle T.
Nonnegative disagreement cost of edge e.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Inconsistent-Triangle Packing Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Semimetric Characterization of Correlation Clusterings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact integral structure underlying the complete-graph semimetric relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{uv}\in\{0,1\}\) be symmetric, satisfy \(x_{uu}=0\), and obey \(x_{uv}\le x_{uw}+x_{wv}\) for all \(u,v,w\). Then \(u\sim v\iff x_{uv}=0\) is an equivalence relation, and its classes form the unique partition \(\Pi\) for which \(x_{uv}=1\) exactly when \(u,v\) are in different clusters. Conversely, every partition produces such a binary semimetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary semimetrics satisfying triangle inequalities are exactly the pair-separation vectors of partitions.
assumptions_latex: The underlying pair set is complete.
The variables are binary, symmetric, and zero on the diagonal.

notation.meaning: Indicator that u and v belong to different clusters.
Zero-distance equivalence relation induced by x.

knowledge_statements.title: Integral Semimetric Characterization of Correlation Clusterings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite strengthening of the complete weighted minimum-disagreement relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succeq0\) satisfy \(G_{uu}=1\) and \(0\le G_{uv}\le1\), put \(x_{uv}=1-G_{uv}\), and impose \(x_{uv}\le x_{uw}+x_{wv}\) for all distinct \(u,v,w\). Minimize \[\sum_{uv\in E^+}w_{uv}x_{uv}+\sum_{uv\in E^-}w_{uv}(1-x_{uv}).\] Every partition is feasible by assigning one orthonormal unit vector to each cluster and using their Gram matrix. Therefore the SDP optimum lower-bounds minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive-semidefinite Gram constraint strengthens the semimetric relaxation while retaining every partition.
assumptions_latex: The signed graph is complete.
Edge weights are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Fractional separation of vertices u and v.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Semimetric Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-complexity boundary for the canonical unweighted complete signed-graph problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing a partition minimizing disagreements is NP-hard even when the signed graph is complete and unweighted. Consequently, unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), no polynomial-time algorithm solves every such instance exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-disagreement correlation clustering is NP-hard even on complete unweighted signed graphs.
assumptions_latex: Every unordered vertex pair has exactly one sign.
All disagreement costs are one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\Longrightarrow\text{no polynomial-time exact algorithm for complete unweighted minimum disagreement}.
knowledge_statements.title: NP-Hardness of Complete-Graph Minimum Disagreement
Correlation-Clustering Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective complementarity does not preserve multiplicative approximation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a complete signed graph on vertex set \(V\) have nonnegative edge weights. For a partition \(\Pi\), let \(D(\Pi)\) be the weight of positive edges crossing clusters plus negative edges within clusters, let \(A(\Pi)\) be the weight of all remaining edges, and let \(W\) be the total edge weight. Define \(\operatorname{OPT}_A:=\max_{\Pi}A(\Pi)\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_D:=\min_{\Pi}D(\Pi)\). Then \(A(\Pi)=W-D(\Pi)\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_A=W-\operatorname{OPT}_D\). Consequently, for \(0<\rho\leq1\), the guarantee \(A(\Pi)\geq\rho\operatorname{OPT}_A\) implies only \[D(\Pi)\leq(1-\rho)W+\rho\operatorname{OPT}_D,\] which need not be a multiplicative approximation for minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agreement and disagreement are exact additive complements, but a multiplicative approximation for maximum agreement need not approximate minimum disagreement multiplicatively.
assumptions_latex: The graph is complete, signed, and has nonnegative edge weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(\Pi)=W-D(\Pi)\), but multiplicative approximation ratios need not transfer through this equality.

notation.meaning: A partition of the vertices into clusters.
Maximum agreement and minimum disagreement values.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: objective complementarity follows directly from the standard complete signed-graph formulation

children.title: Resource Allocation Frontier Family
children.top_down_role: Approximation schemes and constant-factor regimes for numerical packing, assignment, and scheduling.

children.title: Knapsack Frontier
children.top_down_role: Pseudopolynomial structure, scaling schemes, covering variants, and multidimensional boundaries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fractional Bound and Half-Approximation for Zero-One Knapsack
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary relaxation bound and constant-factor algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Discard items with \(w_i>B\), order the rest by nonincreasing \(v_i/w_i\), let \(P\) be the fitting prefix, and let \(k\) be the first nonfitting item. The fractional optimum is at most \(v(P)+v_k\). Hence the better of \(P\) and the most valuable feasible singleton has value at least \(\operatorname{OPT}/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Density sorting yields a fractional upper bound and a one-half approximation after comparison with one item.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\), \(v_i\ge0\), and overweight items are removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Bound and Half-Approximation for Zero-One Knapsack

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation change with a fixed number of capacity dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed \(d\), \(d\)-dimensional zero-one knapsack admits a PTAS. For fixed \(d\ge2\), it has no FPTAS unless \(P=NP\); thus the one-dimensional FPTAS does not extend to two or more capacity coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-dimensional knapsack has a PTAS, but two or more dimensions preclude an FPTAS unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is fixed.
Numerical data are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d=1:\mathrm{FPTAS};\qquad d\ge2:\mathrm{PTAS}\text{ but no FPTAS unless }P=NP.
review_flags: The fixed-dimensional PTAS and FPTAS-impossibility locators are missing.
knowledge_statements.title: Multidimensional Knapsack Scheme Boundary
Knapsack Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical zero-one knapsack with binary-encoded integral weights, values, and capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For items with integral weights \(w_i\geq 0\), integral values \(v_i\geq 0\), and capacity \(B\), zero-one knapsack admits a dynamic program running in \(O(n\sum_i v_i)\) arithmetic steps. For every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), scaling the values yields an algorithm polynomial in the binary input length and \(1/\varepsilon\) that returns a feasible set \(S\) satisfying \[\sum_{i\in S}v_i\geq (1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}.\] Thus the problem has an FPTAS despite being NP-hard; an exact polynomial-time algorithm would imply \(P=NP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-one knapsack is NP-hard but has a pseudopolynomial value dynamic program and an FPTAS obtained by value scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i,v_i,B\) are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
\(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is an FPTAS returning value at least \((1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical pseudopolynomial dynamic programming and value-scaling FPTAS

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pseudopolynomial dynamic program, value-scaling FPTAS, and NP-hardness boundary are mathematically standard and fit the frontier, but no inspectable source supports these nontrivial claims.

children.title: Bin-Packing Frontier
children.top_down_role: Grouping, asymptotic schemes, and absolute-guarantee distinctions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical decreasing-order grouping heuristic for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items by nonincreasing size and places each item in the first open bin with sufficient residual capacity, opening a new bin if necessary. For every instance \(I\), \(\operatorname{FFD}(I)\leq\left\lfloor\frac{11}{9}\operatorname{OPT}(I)+\frac23\right\rfloor\). Consequently FFD has asymptotic ratio \(11/9\) and absolute ratio at most \(3/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-Fit Decreasing is polynomial, has asymptotic ratio 11/9, and attains the three-halves absolute frontier.
assumptions_latex: 0<s_i\leq1.
Bins have capacity 1.

notation.meaning: Number of bins used by First-Fit Decreasing.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Fit Decreasing Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Efficient lower-bound certificates for assessing a packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every feasible packing of items of sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\) uses at least \(\left\lceil\sum_i s_i\right\rceil\) bins and at least \(|\{i:s_i>1/2\}|\) bins. These bounds are independently computable certificates against which an algorithmic packing may be compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total size and the number of items larger than one half give elementary lower bounds on the optimum number of bins.
assumptions_latex: Each bin has capacity 1.
knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Bin-Packing Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Scheme and Absolute Three-Halves Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between asymptotic schemes and absolute approximation for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), one-dimensional bin packing admits a polynomial-time asymptotic approximation scheme producing at most \((1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}+C_\varepsilon\) bins for a constant \(C_\varepsilon\). Unless \(P=NP\), no polynomial-time algorithm has absolute approximation ratio strictly below \(3/2\), since the two-bin versus three-bin gap is NP-hard. Thus an asymptotic scheme does not imply an absolute PTAS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bin packing has asymptotic schemes, but no absolute ratio below three halves unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: 0<s_i\leq1\text{ and bins have capacity }1.
\varepsilon>0\text{ is fixed}.
P\neq NP\text{ for the lower bound}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_A^\infty\text{ can approach }1,\quad\text{but the polynomial-time absolute threshold is at least }3/2.

notation.meaning: Additive constant depending only on epsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Scheme and Absolute Three-Halves Frontier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximation-scheme limitations for binary-encoded one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: One-dimensional bin packing is strongly NP-hard through the 3-Partition restriction. Unless \(P=NP\), it therefore has no pseudopolynomial-time exact algorithm and no FPTAS. This does not conflict with an asymptotic approximation scheme because an asymptotic guarantee permits an additive term that can dominate instances with small optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bin packing is strongly NP-hard and has no pseudopolynomial exact algorithm or FPTAS unless P equals NP, despite admitting asymptotic schemes.
assumptions_latex: Item sizes are rational and binary encoded.
P\neq NP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No pseudopolynomial exact algorithm or FPTAS exists for one-dimensional bin packing}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong NP-Hardness and FPTAS Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation conventions for one-dimensional bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bin-packing algorithm \(A\), its absolute ratio is \(R_A=\sup_I A(I)/\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), while its asymptotic ratio is \(R_A^\infty=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sup_{I:\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq k}A(I)/\operatorname{OPT}(I)\). A bound \(A(I)\leq\rho\operatorname{OPT}(I)+C\) implies \(R_A^\infty\leq\rho\), but need not imply \(R_A\leq\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute ratios include small-optimum instances, whereas asymptotic ratios disregard a fixed additive loss as optimum grows.
assumptions_latex: A(I)\text{ and }\operatorname{OPT}(I)\text{ count unit-capacity bins}.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute and Asymptotic Bin-Packing Ratios
Bin-Packing Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic and absolute guarantees for one-dimensional unit-capacity bin packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given item sizes \(s_i\in(0,1]\), for every \(\varepsilon>0\) one-dimensional bin packing has an asymptotic approximation scheme producing a packing with at most \[(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}+C_\varepsilon\] bins, where \(C_\varepsilon\) depends only on \(\varepsilon\). In contrast, unless \(P=NP\), no polynomial-time algorithm has absolute approximation ratio strictly smaller than \(3/2\): such an algorithm would distinguish instances packable into two bins from instances requiring at least three. Hence an asymptotic scheme does not imply an absolute PTAS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bin packing admits asymptotic schemes, while an absolute ratio below three halves is impossible unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: Each bin has capacity \(1\).
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asymptotic ratios approach \(1\), but the absolute approximation threshold is at least \(3/2\) unless \(P=NP\).

notation.meaning: Additive constant depending only on accuracy.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical asymptotic-scheme and partition-gap frontier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic-scheme statement and absolute 3/2 barrier are plausible and appropriately distinguish asymptotic from absolute guarantees, but both require specific authoritative locators.

children.title: Makespan Scheduling Frontiers
children.top_down_role: Approximation across identical, related, and unrelated machines.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical greedy guarantees for identical parallel machines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each next job to a least-loaded machine. For \(m\) identical machines, any list order gives \(C_{\max}\le(2-1/m)\operatorname{OPT}\). Ordering jobs first by nonincreasing processing time gives \(C_{\max}\le(4/3-1/(3m))\operatorname{OPT}\) for \(m\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-loaded list scheduling has ratio two-minus-one-over-m, improved by LPT ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge2\) identical machines.
Jobs are independent and nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.title: List-Scheduling Bounds on Identical Machines

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Workload and Largest-Job Makespan Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary approximation certificates for identical machines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every schedule for \(P\|C_{\max}\) satisfies \(C_{\max}\ge L:=\max\{\max_jp_j,(\sum_jp_j)/m\}\). Therefore a schedule of makespan at most \(\alpha L\) is an \(\alpha\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest job and average workload are universal makespan lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Processing times are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Workload and Largest-Job Makespan Lower Bounds
Makespan Scheduling Frontiers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nonpreemptive makespan minimization across standard machine environments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonpreemptive makespan minimization, both identical machines \(P\|C_{\max}\) and uniformly related machines \(Q\|C_{\max}\) admit polynomial-time approximation schemes: for every fixed \(\delta>0\), the returned schedule has makespan at most \((1+\delta)\operatorname{OPT}\). For unrelated machines \(R\|C_{\max}\), linear-programming rounding gives a polynomial-time \(2\)-approximation. Moreover, for every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), a polynomial-time \((3/2-\varepsilon)\)-approximation for unrelated machines would imply \(P=NP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical and related-machine makespan have PTASs; unrelated-machine makespan has a two-approximation and a three-halves hardness barrier.
assumptions_latex: Jobs are scheduled nonpreemptively.
Processing times are nonnegative rational numbers.
\(\delta>0\) is fixed for the approximation schemes.
\(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) is fixed for the hardness statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The frontier changes from a PTAS on \(P\) and \(Q\) machines to constant-factor approximation and hardness on \(R\) machines.

notation.meaning: Identical, uniformly related, and unrelated machine environments.
PTAS accuracy and hardness-gap parameters, respectively.

children.title: Time-Sensitive Scheduling Frontiers
children.top_down_role: Rounding, greedy, and release-date regimes for sequencing objectives.

children.title: Completion-Time Scheduling Frontier
children.top_down_role: Approximation regimes for aggregate or weighted completion objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shortest-Processing-Time Rules for Total Completion Time
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted single- and identical-parallel-machine exact regimes.

On identical parallel machines, dispatching jobs in nondecreasing processing-time order to a currently least-loaded machine is optimal for \(P\|\sum_jC_j\).

Processing times are positive.

Completion-Time Scheduling Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact single-machine weighted-completion-time regime without release dates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For jobs available at time zero on one nonpreemptive machine, initialize the unscheduled set as all jobs and order them by nondecreasing ratio \(p_j/w_j\), treating \(w_j=0\) as ratio \(+\infty\). Process jobs consecutively in this order without idle time and output the resulting schedule. This Smith-rule schedule minimizes \[\sum_j w_jC_j\] over all nonpreemptive single-machine schedules. Equivalently, jobs with positive weights appear in nonincreasing order of \(w_j/p_j\); ties may be resolved arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without release dates, sorting jobs by processing-time-to-weight ratio exactly minimizes total weighted completion time on one machine.
assumptions_latex: \(p_j>0\) and \(w_j\geq 0\) for every job.
All jobs are available at time \(0\).
Scheduling is nonpreemptive on one machine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ratio-ordered schedule belongs to \(\arg\min\sum_j w_jC_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and optimality claim correctly state Smith's rule for the specified single-machine regime, but its nontrivial optimality theorem lacks an inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maximum-lateness and all-deadlines-feasible regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\|L_{\max}\), where \(L_j=C_j-d_j\), nondecreasing due-date order minimizes \(L_{\max}\). Consequently, an all-on-time schedule exists exactly when the EDD schedule satisfies \(C_j\le d_j\) for every job.

assumptions_latex: All jobs are available at time zero on one nonpreemptive machine.
Processing times are positive.

Deadline Scheduling Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between unweighted and weighted late-job minimization on one machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\|\sum_j U_j\), sort jobs by nondecreasing deadlines and scan that order. Whenever the accumulated processing time exceeds the current deadline, remove from the current prefix a job of maximum processing time; append all removed jobs after the retained jobs. The resulting schedule minimizes the number of late jobs in polynomial time. If the objective becomes \(\sum_j w_jU_j\) with arbitrary nonnegative weights, the problem is NP-hard, so the unweighted deletion rule does not extend to an exact polynomial-time algorithm unless \(P=NP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moore–Hodgson scheduling exactly minimizes the number of late jobs, but arbitrary lateness weights make the problem NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: All jobs are available at time \(0\) on one nonpreemptive machine.
\(p_j>0\) and deadlines \(d_j\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unweighted late-job minimization is polynomially solvable, whereas its weighted extension is NP-hard.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Release-date total completion time is NP-hard without preemption but exactly solvable with preemption.
assumptions_latex: Processing times and release dates are nonnegative rational inputs.
review_flags: The NP-hardness claim requires an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preemptive tractable regime for unweighted total completion time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1|r_j,\mathrm{pmtn}|\sum_jC_j\), always process an available unfinished job of minimum remaining processing time, preempting when a job with smaller remaining work arrives. This SRPT schedule minimizes \(\sum_jC_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With release dates and cost-free preemption, SRPT exactly minimizes total completion time.
assumptions_latex: There is one machine.
Jobs have release dates and positive processing times.
Preemption is permitted without cost.
knowledge_statements.title: SRPT Optimality with Release Dates
Release-Date Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Release dates can make intentional idling necessary for completion-time objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(M>3\), consider two unweighted jobs on one nonpreemptive machine: job \(a\) has \((r_a,p_a)=(0,M)\), and job \(b\) has \((r_b,p_b)=(1,1)\). Every work-conserving schedule starts \(a\) at time zero and has total completion time \(C_a+C_b=2M+1\). A schedule that idles until time one, executes \(b\), and then executes \(a\) has total completion time \(M+4\), which is optimal. Thus release dates invalidate the no-idling property, and the work-conserving ratio tends to \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With release dates, deliberately idling can nearly halve total completion time compared with every work-conserving schedule.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is an integer greater than \(3\).
The machine is single and scheduling is nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The best work-conserving schedule has ratio \((2M+1)/(M+4)\to 2\) against the optimum.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit two-job construction is directly checkable

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Profit-maximizing generalized assignment has a tight one-minus-one-over-e approximation threshold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical profit-maximization variant.

Assignments with \(p_{ij}>b_i\) may be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job is packed into at most one machine, with machine-dependent size and profit and one capacity per machine.
assumptions_latex: \(I,J\) are finite.
All sizes, capacities, and profits are nonnegative.

Generalized Assignment Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shmoys–Tardos-type rounding for the cost-constrained assignment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) be finite sets of machines and jobs, let \(T\geq0\), and let \(p_{ij},c_{ij}\geq0\) for every \((i,j)\in I\times J\). Suppose \(x_{ij}\geq0\) satisfies \(\sum_{i\in I}x_{ij}=1\) for every \(j\in J\), \(\sum_{j\in J}p_{ij}x_{ij}\leq T\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(x_{ij}=0\) whenever \(p_{ij}>T\). There is a polynomial-time rounding to an integral assignment \(\sigma:J\to I\) such that \[\sum_{j\in J}c_{\sigma(j)j}\leq\sum_{i\in I,\,j\in J}c_{ij}x_{ij}\] and, for every \(i\in I\), \[\sum_{j:\,\sigma(j)=i}p_{ij}\leq T+eta_i\leq2T,\] where \(\beta_i:=\max\{p_{ij}:\sigma(j)=i\}\) if machine \(i\) receives a job and \(\beta_i:=0\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible fractional generalized assignment can be rounded without increasing cost while increasing every machine load to at most twice the target.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite.
\(T\geq0\), and all processing times and assignment costs are nonnegative.
The displayed fractional assignment constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An integral assignment of cost no greater than the fractional cost and makespan at most \(2T\) exists and is computable in polynomial time.

notation.meaning: Fraction of job j assigned to machine i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted MAX-SAT Objective and Clause Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted weighted Boolean maximum-satisfiability benchmark used by the local approximation records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted MAX-SAT instance is a finite multiset \(\mathcal C\) of disjunctive Boolean clauses with weights \(w_C\ge0\). For an assignment \(a\), \[\operatorname{val}(a)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}w_C\mathbf 1[a\models C],\qquad \operatorname{OPT}=\max_a\operatorname{val}(a).\] An empty clause is never satisfied and may be discarded without changing the objective. A clause containing complementary literals is always satisfied and may be removed after recording its weight as an additive constant. Repeated occurrences of a literal may be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MAX-SAT maximizes satisfied clause weight, with explicit normalization for empty, tautological, and repeated-literal clauses.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C\text{ is finite}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Standard MAX-SAT Clause Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual of the accepted standard weighted MAX-SAT LP after writing literal sums in terms of fractional truth variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_C\) be the negative literals of clause \(C\). Write the primal constraint as \(z_C-\sum_{x_i\in C}y_i+\sum_{\neg x_i\in C}y_i\le |N_C|\), together with \(z_C\le1\), \(y_i\le1\), and nonnegativity. Its dual is \[\min\ \sum_C |N_C|a_C+\sum_C b_C+\sum_i u_i\] subject to \[a_C+b_C\ge w_C\quad(C),\qquad -\sum_{C:x_i\in C}a_C+\sum_{C:\neg x_i\in C}a_C+u_i\ge0\quad(i),\qquad a,b,u\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard clause LP has a covering dual whose variables price literal-sum constraints, clause caps, and truth-variable upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-width-one specialization with nonnegative clause weights.

The resulting value is \(\sum_i\max\{W_i^+,W_i^-\}=\operatorname{OPT}\), and the algorithm runs in time linear in the explicit instance size.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Satisfiability versus Maximum-Satisfiability Boundary at Width Two
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity distinction between deciding whether all binary clauses can be satisfied and maximizing satisfied clause weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility of a Boolean formula whose clauses have at most two literals is decidable in polynomial time by the implication-graph algorithm for \(2\)-SAT. In contrast, optimizing the number or nonnegative weight of satisfied clauses is NP-hard already for MAX-2-SAT. Thus polynomial solvability of \(2\)-SAT does not imply exact polynomial solvability of its maximum-satisfaction variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-SAT feasibility is polynomial-time, but MAX-2-SAT optimization is NP-hard, so their complexity frontiers differ.

Maximum Satisfiability Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline weighted MAX-SAT guarantee from random assignment and derandomization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each nonempty clause \(C\) have nonnegative weight \(w_C\), contain \(k_C\) distinct variables, and contain no complementary literal pair. Let \(\operatorname{OPT}\) be the maximum satisfied clause weight over all truth assignments. Independently assign every variable uniformly in \(\{0,1\}\). Clause \(C\) is satisfied with probability \(1-2^{-k_C}\), so the expected satisfied weight is \[\sum_C w_C(1-2^{-k_C})\geq\frac12\sum_Cw_C\geq\frac12\operatorname{OPT}.\] Fixing variables successively to preserve conditional expectation produces a deterministic polynomial-time assignment with satisfied weight at least \(\operatorname{OPT}/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform random assignment satisfies at least half the total clause weight in expectation, and conditional expectations yield a deterministic one-half approximation.
assumptions_latex: Clause weights are nonnegative.
Every clause is nonempty and has distinct, noncomplementary literals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Coloring Complexity Boundary at Two Colors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact polynomial-time bipartite coloring and fixed-palette coloring from three colors onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whether \(\chi(G)\le2\) can be decided in linear time by breadth-first search, which returns a proper two-coloring or an odd-cycle obstruction. For every fixed integer \(k\ge3\), deciding whether \(\chi(G)\le k\) is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact two-colorability is efficiently certified, whereas exact k-colorability is NP-complete for every fixed k at least three.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph.
\(k\ge3\) is fixed for the NP-completeness statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \chi(G)\le2\text{ is decidable in linear time},\qquad k\ge3:\ \{G:\chi(G)\le k\}\text{ is NP-complete}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance conventions for general and promised vertex-coloring regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If algorithm \(A\) returns a proper coloring using \(q_A(G)\) colors, a multiplicative guarantee has the form \(q_A(G)\le\rho(n)\chi(G)\), an additive guarantee has the form \(q_A(G)\le\chi(G)+a(n)\), and a promised-palette guarantee has the form \(\chi(G)\le k\Rightarrow q_A(G)\le f_k(n)\). These conventions are not interchangeable with comparable parameters: conversion requires explicit bounds on \(\chi(G)\), and a promised-palette result applies only to its promised instance class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative ratios, additive excess colors, and palette bounds for promised-colorable graphs are distinct guarantees whose parameters cannot be compared without explicit conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph.
The algorithm returns a proper vertex coloring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_A\le\rho\chi,\quad q_A\le\chi+a,\quad(\chi\le k\Rightarrow q_A\le f_k)\text{ are distinct performance conventions}.

notation.meaning: Number of colors returned by algorithm A.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, given an \(n\)-vertex graph satisfying \(\chi(G)\le 3\), returns a proper coloring using \(O(n^{3/14}\sqrt{\log n})\) colors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A promised three-colorable graph can be properly colored in randomized polynomial time with roughly n to the 3/14 colors.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices.

notation.meaning: Number of colors returned by the algorithm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between promised-colorable and unrestricted coloring guarantees.

Consequently, a theorem of the form \(\chi(G)\le k\Rightarrow q_A(G)\le f_k(n)\) imposes no conclusion on \(K_n\) and cannot alone establish an unrestricted multiplicative or additive approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete graphs show that a palette bound proved only for k-colorable inputs gives no unrestricted coloring guarantee.
assumptions_latex: k\ge1\text{ is fixed}.
n>k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary optimality certificate for finite simple vertex-coloring instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If K\subseteq V is a clique and \varphi:V\to\{1,\ldots,q\} is a proper coloring, then every vertex of K receives a distinct color, so |K|\leq\chi(G)\leq q. Consequently, |K|=q certifies simultaneously that K is a maximum clique and \varphi is an optimal coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique gives a chromatic lower bound, a proper coloring gives an upper bound, and equal bounds certify an optimal coloring.

K\text{ is supplied explicitly and is a clique}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant Multiplicative Error Can Have Unbounded Additive Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation between multiplicative and additive coloring performance measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G_k be the complete k-partite graph with two vertices in every part. Then \chi(G_k)=k. Coloring every vertex with its own color is proper and uses 2k colors, giving multiplicative ratio 2 but additive excess k. Thus a constant multiplicative guarantee does not imply a constant additive guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On complete k-partite graphs with two vertices per part, a proper 2k-coloring has constant ratio two but additive error k.
assumptions_latex: k\geq1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured sparse-graph coloring guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every nonempty subgraph of \(G\) has a vertex of degree at most \(d\), iterative minimum-degree deletion produces a degeneracy ordering. Greedily coloring vertices in reverse deletion order uses at most \(d+1\) colors. With bucket-based degree maintenance, the ordering and coloring are computable in \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A d-degenerate graph can be colored with at most d+1 colors in linear time by reverse greedy coloring.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a finite simple graph}.
d\text{ is the degeneracy of }G.

Graph Coloring Frontiers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General-graph chromatic-number approximation; promised graph classes require separate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\), greedy coloring in any vertex order uses at most \(\Delta(G)+1\leq n\) colors and therefore supplies a polynomial-time factor at most \(n/\chi(G)\). Conversely, for every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), approximating \(\chi(G)\) within a factor \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\) on arbitrary graphs is NP-hard. Thus, unless \(P=NP\), general graph coloring admits no polynomial-time \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\)-approximation, while promises such as bounded degree, density, or bounded chromatic number define distinct approximation regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General graph coloring has a trivial broad guarantee and is NP-hard to approximate within an almost linear factor.

\(0<\varepsilon<1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A polynomial-time \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\)-approximation for arbitrary-graph chromatic number would imply \(P=NP\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary for algorithms guaranteeing only inclusion maximality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_n\) be the disjoint union of an isolated vertex \(v\) and a clique \(K_{n-1}\). Then \(\{v\}\) is an inclusion-maximal clique of size \(1\), while \(\omega(G_n)=n-1\). Thus returning an arbitrary maximal clique can have approximation ratio \(n-1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\Delta=\Delta(\overline G)=n-1-\delta(G)\). Greedily construct an inclusion-maximal clique \(K\) of \(G\). Clique Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum clique approximation on unrestricted finite simple graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be an \(n\)-vertex simple graph and let \(\omega(G)\) denote its maximum clique size. For every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), it is NP-hard to compute in polynomial time a clique \(K\) satisfying \[|K|\geq\frac{\omega(G)}{n^{1-\varepsilon}}.\] Hence, unless \(P=NP\), maximum clique has no polynomial-time \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\)-approximation on general graphs. This near-linear hardness applies to multiplicative objective approximation and does not preclude stronger guarantees on restricted graph classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum clique is NP-hard to approximate within an almost linear factor on unrestricted graphs.

\(0<\varepsilon<1\) is fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singleton Approximation Baseline for Maximum Independent Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted maximum independent set on a nonempty finite simple graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty n-vertex graph G, returning any vertex produces an independent set I with |I|=1 and therefore |I|\geq\alpha(G)/n. Thus this is a deterministic polynomial-time n-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Returning one vertex gives the elementary n-approximation baseline for maximum independent set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent-Set Lower and Clique-Partition Upper Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary verifiable bounds for unweighted maximum independent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A listed set \(I\subseteq V\) certifies \(\alpha(G)\ge|I|\) when no two distinct vertices of \(I\) are adjacent. A partition \(V=Q_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}Q_q\) into cliques certifies \(\alpha(G)\le q\). Hence \[|I|\le\alpha(G)\le q,\] and equality \(|I|=q\) certifies that \(I\) is maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit independent set gives a lower bound, a clique partition gives an upper bound, and equal bounds certify maximum size.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph.
The independent set and clique partition are supplied explicitly.
