knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Independent Set Can Be Almost Trivially Small
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary for algorithms guaranteeing only inclusion maximality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the star \(G_n=K_{1,n-1}\) with center \(c\), the set \(\{c\}\) is an inclusion-maximal independent set of size \(1\), while all \(n-1\) leaves form an independent set and \(\alpha(G_n)=n-1\). Thus returning an arbitrary maximal independent set can have approximation ratio \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The center of a star is a maximal independent set of size one, while all leaves form an independent set of size n minus one.
assumptions_latex: n\ge3

notation.meaning: Star with one center and n-1 leaves

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Independent Set Can Be Almost Trivially Small

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Degree Approximation for Maximum Independent Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy structured-graph guarantee parameterized by maximum degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a nonempty graph \(G\) of maximum degree \(\Delta\), greedily construct an inclusion-maximal independent set \(I\). Maximality implies that the closed neighborhoods of vertices in \(I\) cover \(V\), and each has at most \(\Delta+1\) vertices. Hence \(|I|\ge n/(\Delta+1)\). Since \(\alpha(G)\le n\), this is a polynomial-time \((\Delta+1)\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any maximal independent set is a Delta-plus-one approximation on graphs of maximum degree Delta.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a nonempty finite simple graph}
\Delta=\Delta(G)
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Degree Approximation for Maximum Independent Set
Independent-Set Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation-preserving complement-graph equivalence with maximum clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), a set \(S\subseteq V\) is independent in \(G\) if and only if it is a clique in the complement graph \(\overline G\). Consequently, \[\alpha(G)=\omega(\overline G).\] Graph complementation is polynomial-time, preserves the number of vertices, and preserves feasible-set cardinalities. Therefore every multiplicative approximation guarantee or hardness threshold for maximum clique transfers unchanged to maximum independent set. In particular, for every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), a polynomial-time \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\)-approximation for maximum independent set would imply \(P=NP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementation exactly converts independent sets to cliques and transfers their approximation guarantees and hardness thresholds without loss.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph with \(n\) vertices.
\(0<\varepsilon<1\) is fixed for the hardness consequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(G)=\omega(\overline G)\), with approximation ratios preserved by complementation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: complement equivalence is immediate from the definitions; hardness transfer uses the clique frontier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact approximation transfer between clique and independent set under graph complementation, together with the boundary of that transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple graph and let \(\overline G\) be its complement. A set \(S\subseteq V\) is a clique in \(G\) if and only if it is an independent set in \(\overline G\). Consequently, \(\omega(G)=\alpha(\overline G)\), and complementation transfers every polynomial-time \(\rho(|V|)\)-approximation for maximum clique into a polynomial-time \(\rho(|V|)\)-approximation for maximum independent set, and conversely. This feasible-set identity alone supplies no ratio-preserving transfer for an objective whose value depends on induced edge density rather than only on the selected vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph complementation exactly transfers clique and independent-set approximation ratios. The same identity does not by itself preserve approximation ratios for induced edge-density objectives.

children.title: Shortest-Superstring Frontier
children.top_down_role: Overlap-based approximation and compression-related hardness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit shortest common superstring, including fixed finite-alphabet restrictions where supported by the hardness theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a constant \varepsilon_0>0 for which it is NP-hard to distinguish instances with a common superstring of length at most L from instances whose every common superstring has length greater than \((1+\varepsilon_0)L\). Consequently, shortest superstring has no polynomial-time approximation scheme unless P=NP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortest superstring is APX-hard and has no PTAS unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: Input strings are represented explicitly.
The alphabet restriction must match the cited hardness theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\ne NP\Rightarrow\) shortest superstring has no PTAS.
knowledge_statements.title: APX-Hardness Boundary for Shortest Superstring

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed Triangle Inequality of Overlap Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed overlap distance on a substring-free input family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After deleting duplicate and contained strings, define d(x,y)=|y|-|\operatorname{ov}(x,y)|, where \operatorname{ov}(x,y) is the longest suffix of x that is a prefix of y. Then d(x,z)\leq d(x,y)+d(y,z) for all remaining strings x,y,z.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additional-length overlap cost is a directed metric on the reduced string family.
assumptions_latex: No retained input string is a substring of another retained input string.

notation.meaning: additional length for appending y after x

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Triangle Inequality of Overlap Distance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preprocessing and ordering representation for shortest common superstring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Deleting duplicates and every input string contained in another preserves the optimum. For a permutation \pi of the remaining strings, appending each next string using the overlap with its predecessor produces a feasible superstring of length |s_{\pi(1)}|+\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}d(s_{\pi(i)},s_{\pi(i+1)}). Minimizing this expression over permutations yields the shortest-superstring optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After containment preprocessing, shortest superstring is represented by a minimum directed overlap-ordering cost.
assumptions_latex: The input is a finite explicit set of strings.
Containment and suffix-prefix overlaps are computed exactly.

notation.meaning: additional length incurred by appending y after x

knowledge_statements.title: Containment Reduction and Overlap-Ordering Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical non-sharp upper bound for greedy overlap merging after containment preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Delete duplicates and strings contained in another input string. Repeatedly select two current strings having maximum suffix-prefix overlap, replace them by their shortest overlap merge, and continue until one string remains. Under arbitrary tie breaking, the resulting common superstring has length at most \(4\operatorname{OPT}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated maximum-overlap merging has the classical factor-four guarantee for shortest superstring.
assumptions_latex: The input is a finite explicitly represented string family.
Duplicates and contained strings are removed.
Overlaps and merges are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Maximum-Overlap Greedy Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modern constant-factor upper bound for explicitly represented shortest common superstring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, for every finite explicitly represented string family \(S\), returns a common superstring \(T\) satisfying \(|T|\le\tfrac32\operatorname{OPT}(S)\). Duplicate strings and strings contained in another input string may first be removed without changing the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortest superstring admits a polynomial-time three-halves approximation after harmless containment preprocessing.
assumptions_latex: The input is a finite explicitly represented string family.
Containment and overlaps are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Three-Halves Approximation for Shortest Superstring

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially computable overlap lower bound after containment preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After deleting duplicates and contained strings, let \(L=\sum_{s\in S}|s|\), weight each directed arc \((x,y)\) by \(|\operatorname{ov}(x,y)|\), and let \(C^*\) be the maximum total weight of a directed cycle cover. Every overlap ordering is a Hamiltonian path, which can be closed by one nonnegative-weight arc and therefore has overlap weight at most \(C^*\). Consequently \(\operatorname{OPT}(S)\ge L-C^*\). A maximum-weight cycle cover is computable as an assignment problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total retained-string length minus maximum cycle-cover overlap is a polynomially computable lower bound on shortest-superstring length.
assumptions_latex: Duplicates and strings contained in another input string have been removed.
Suffix-prefix overlaps are computed exactly.

notation.meaning: Maximum total overlap weight of a directed cycle cover.
Longest suffix of x that is a prefix of y.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Cycle-Cover Compression Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Subset Dynamic Program for Shortest Superstring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exponential-time algorithm after containment preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After deleting duplicates and contained strings, index the remaining strings by \([m]\), let \(d(i,j)=|s_j|-|\operatorname{ov}(s_i,s_j)|\), and define \(D[\{j\},j]=|s_j|\) and \[D[U,j]=\min_{i\in U\setminus\{j\}}\bigl(D[U\setminus\{j\},i]+d(i,j)\bigr).\] Then \(\min_jD[[m],j]=\operatorname{OPT}(S)\); predecessor pointers recover an optimal superstring. After overlap computation, the algorithm uses \(O(m^2 2^m)\) time and \(O(m2^m)\) space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Held–Karp-style subset dynamic program computes an exact shortest superstring in exponential time.
assumptions_latex: Duplicates and strings contained in another input string have been removed.
All suffix-prefix overlaps are computed exactly.

notation.meaning: Minimum merged length for exactly the strings in U, ending with j.
Additional length incurred by appending j after i.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Subset Dynamic Program for Shortest Superstring

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially solvable two-string specialization, including containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two strings \(x,y\), if one is a substring of the other, the longer string is an optimal common superstring. Otherwise let \(a=|\operatorname{ov}(x,y)|\) and \(b=|\operatorname{ov}(y,x)|\). An optimal common superstring is the shorter of the two overlap merges, and \(\operatorname{OPT}(\{x,y\})=|x|+|y|-\max\{a,b\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two strings, use the longer string under containment; otherwise merge in the direction with greater suffix-prefix overlap.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ and }y\text{ are finite explicitly represented strings}.
Suffix-prefix overlaps are computed exactly.

notation.meaning: Length of the longest suffix of x that is a prefix of y
Length of the longest suffix of y that is a prefix of x

Shortest-Superstring Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation frontier for the minimum-length common-superstring problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(S\) of strings over a finite alphabet, let \(\operatorname{OPT}(S)\) be the minimum length of a string containing every member of \(S\) as a contiguous substring. The polynomial-time approximation frontier is \(\rho_{\mathrm{SSS}}=\inf_A\sup_S |A(S)|/\operatorname{OPT}(S)\), where the infimum ranges over polynomial-time algorithms returning feasible superstrings. An upper bound \(r\) is established by an algorithm with ratio at most \(r\); a lower frontier bound \(h\) requires a complexity assumption excluding every polynomial-time ratio below \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The shortest-superstring frontier is the infimum worst-case approximation ratio achievable by polynomial-time algorithms, paired with complexity-based lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Input strings and algorithm outputs are represented explicitly.
\(\operatorname{OPT}(S)>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a covering-form minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal relaxation \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\). Any explicitly represented vector \(y\) satisfying the dual inequalities is a feasible dual certificate. Its validity is checked by evaluating \(y\ge0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\). For every primal-feasible \(x\), weak duality gives \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le c^{\mathsf T}x\); hence \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) is a verifiable lower bound on the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible vector is a directly checkable lower-bound certificate for every feasible solution of the covering-form primal relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) have compatible finite dimensions.
The primal and dual values are finite where invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le \operatorname{OPT}_{P}\le c^{\mathsf T}x\) for dual-feasible \(y\) and primal-feasible \(x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality from a feasible dual lower bound matching a feasible primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the covering-form primal and its dual, let \(x\) be primal feasible and \(y\) dual feasible. If \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\), weak duality implies \[b^{\mathsf T}y\le\operatorname{OPT}_P\le c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y.\] Hence both vectors are optimal. If their values differ, the difference is only a certified upper-minus-lower gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and dual vectors with equal values certify optimality; unequal values certify only an interval.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is primal feasible
\(y\) is dual feasible
Both displayed objectives are finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}x=b^{\mathsf T}y\Rightarrow x\text{ and }y\text{ are optimal}\)
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Equality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic complexity of checking an explicitly represented covering-form dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given explicit rational \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\), and \(y\in\mathbb Q^m\), dual feasibility is checked by testing \(y\ge0\), computing \(A^{\mathsf T}y\), and testing \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\). This uses \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\) rational arithmetic operations and polynomial bit complexity in the total encoding length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One sparse matrix-vector product and componentwise comparisons verify an explicit rational dual certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A,c,y\) are explicitly represented rational data
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility is checkable in \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\) rational arithmetic operations.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero entries of A

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Dual-Certificate Verification Cost

children.title: Scaled-Dual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Comparison certificates supported by adjusted or rescaled dual objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled-Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation certificate obtained by scaling an approximately feasible dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the covering primal \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\), suppose \(\alpha>0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le\alpha c\). Then \(y/\alpha\) is dual feasible, so \(b^{\mathsf T}y/\alpha\le\operatorname{OPT}_{P}\). If an integral feasible solution \(x^{I}\) also satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}x^{I}\le b^{\mathsf T}y\), the pair \((x^{I},y)\) certifies \(c^{\mathsf T}x^{I}\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{P}\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{I}\). All displayed inequalities are directly checkable from the instance and certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximately dual-feasible vector, paired with a sufficiently cheap integral solution, certifies an approximation ratio equal to the scaling factor.
assumptions_latex: The integral feasible region is contained in the primal relaxation.
\(c^{\mathsf T}x^{I}\) is finite.

children.title: Dual-Scaling Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting when scaled dual evidence supports a guarantee.

assumptions_latex: The primal is written as \(Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual scaling is valid only when \(\alpha>0\) and \(y/\alpha\) is feasible for the correctly derived dual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary sign, feasibility, and positive-scaling conditions for dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scaled-dual conclusion requires \(\alpha>0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le\alpha c\) for the covering-form primal. Dropping the last inequality is unsound: with \(A=b=c=[1]\), the primal optimum is \(1\), but \(y=2\) falsely claims the lower bound \(2\). Dropping nonnegativity is also unsound: with \(A=[0]\), \(b=[-1]\), and \(c=[0]\), the primal optimum is \(0\), while \(y=-1\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) yet gives the false lower bound \(b^{\mathsf T}y=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling and every dual-feasibility condition are essential; explicit one-variable instances produce false lower bounds when constraints are removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Scaling Validity Boundaries

children.title: Relaxation-Value Certificates
children.top_down_role: Comparison with tractable relaxation values.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Value Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation comparison against a tractable lower relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_I\subseteq F_R\) be the feasible regions of a minimization problem and its tractable relaxation, with common objective \(c\). Define \(L=\min_{x\in F_R}c(x)\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_I=\min_{x\in F_I}c(x)\). A relaxation-value certificate consists of a certified value \(L\) and an integral feasible solution \(z\in F_I\). Since \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}_I\), the checkable inequality \(c(z)\le\rho L\), for \(\rho\ge1\), certifies \(c(z)\le\rho\operatorname{OPT}_I\). Certification of \(L\) may use exact relaxation optimization or matching primal and dual relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible integral solution costing at most rho times a certified relaxation lower bound has approximation ratio at most rho.
assumptions_latex: \(F_I\subseteq F_R\).
\(L\) and \(\operatorname{OPT}_I\) are finite and positive.

children.title: Combinatorial Lower-Bound Witnesses
children.top_down_role: Packing, covering, matching, and decomposition witnesses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of disjoint witness blocks using bounded element congestion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(F)=\sum_{u\in F}c_u\) with \(c_u\ge0\). Suppose \(c(F\cap B_i)\ge\lambda_i\) for every feasible \(F\). If \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i:u\in B_i}w_i\le1\) for every \(u\), then \[c(F)\ge\sum_iw_i c(F\cap B_i)\ge\sum_iw_i\lambda_i.\] Thus \(\sum_iw_i\lambda_i\le\operatorname{OPT}\), even when the blocks overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping obstructions combine validly when nonnegative weights load each ground element by at most one.
assumptions_latex: Every local lower bound is valid for every feasible solution
\(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i:u\in B_i}w_i\le1\)

knowledge_statements.title: Fractionally Weighted Overlapping Witnesses

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When a mathematical witness is also a succinct computational certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A listed family \((B_i,\lambda_i,w_i)_i\) is polynomially checkable only if its encoding is polynomial in the instance size and a verifier can check nonnegativity, disjointness or element-load inequalities, and every asserted local bound in polynomial time. Universal validity of \(c(F\cap B_i)\ge\lambda_i\) alone does not make the assertion efficiently verifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid combinatorial bound is a computational certificate only when its encoding and local claims are efficiently checkable.
assumptions_latex: Certificate complexity is measured in binary input length under deterministic verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mathematical validity alone does not imply polynomial-time certificate verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Efficient Verifiability Boundary
Combinatorial Lower-Bound Witnesses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive lower bounds assembled from disjoint combinatorial obstructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization problem have nonnegative additive cost \(c(F)=\sum_{u\in F}c_u\) on a ground set \(U\). A combinatorial lower-bound witness is a family of pairwise disjoint sets \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\subseteq U\), together with locally verifiable bounds \(c(F\cap B_i)\ge\lambda_i\) for every feasible \(F\). Disjointness and nonnegativity imply \(c(F)\ge\sum_{i=1}^k c(F\cap B_i)\ge\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\). Thus the witness certifies \(\sum_i\lambda_i\le\operatorname{OPT}\); packings, matchings, and decompositions instantiate the sets and local bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint obstructions with independently verifiable mandatory costs add to a certified lower bound on every feasible solution.

children.title: Gap Upper-Bound Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic inequality certificate for a minimization locality-gap upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be locally optimal for a minimization neighborhood \(N\), and let \(O\) be globally optimal. Suppose there are neighbors \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\in N(S)\), weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\), and constants \(A>0\), \(B\ge A\) such that \(A c(S)-B c(O)\le\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i(c(S)-c(S_i))\). Since local optimality gives \(c(S)-c(S_i)\le0\), it follows that \(c(S)\le(B/A)c(O)\). If such an aggregation exists for every local optimum and global optimum, the locality gap is at most \(B/A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted aggregation of valid local-exchange inequalities certifies a locality-gap upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(S_i\in N(S)\) for every \(i\).
\(S\) is locally optimal for minimization, so \(c(S)\le c(S_i)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized counterpart of uniform deterministic rounding for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each minimization instance \(I\), let \(x^*\) be an optimal solution of a relaxation with value \(L(I)>0\). If randomized rounding returns an integral feasible \(Y\) with probability one and satisfies \(\mathbb E[c_I(Y)]\le\rho c_I(x^*)\), then \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\le\rho L(I)\), so the relaxation's integrality gap is at most \(\rho\). If the relaxation and rounding procedure are polynomial-time, the procedure is a polynomial-time \(\rho\)-approximation in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected rho-loss randomized rounding proves an integrality-gap upper bound and, when efficiently implementable, gives a rho-approximation in expectation.
assumptions_latex: The random output is integral and feasible with probability one.
The expectation exists and \(L(I)>0\).

Gap Upper-Bound Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform rounding bound implying an integrality-gap upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each minimization instance \(I\), let \(F_I^{R}\) be a relaxation containing its integral feasible region, and let \(L(I)=\min_{x\in F_I^{R}}c_I(x)>0\). Suppose a polynomial-time rounding or decomposition map \(R_I\) sends every \(x\in F_I^{R}\) to an integral feasible solution and satisfies \(c_I(R_I(x))\le\rho c_I(x)\). Applying the map to an optimal relaxation solution yields \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\le\rho L(I)\). Therefore the integrality gap of this relaxation over the instance class is at most \(\rho\), and the map gives a \(\rho\)-approximation whenever the relaxation is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform rho-loss rounding map simultaneously proves an integrality-gap upper bound and a rho-approximation algorithm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic witness families for relaxation gaps or locality gaps, with the two ratio conventions stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a minimization problem and a sequence of instances \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) whose sizes tend to infinity. For a relaxation with positive optimum \(L(I_n)\le\operatorname{OPT}(I_n)\), the sequence is a relaxation-gap family of asymptotic factor \(\gamma\in[1,\infty]\) when \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{OPT}(I_n)/L(I_n)=\gamma\). For a specified neighborhood system \(N\), let \(W_N(I)\) be the supremum of \(c_I(x)\) over feasible solutions \(x\) that are locally optimal under \(N\). The sequence is a locality-gap family of asymptotic factor \(\gamma\) when \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}W_N(I_n)/\operatorname{OPT}(I_n)=\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap instance family is a growing sequence witnessing an asymptotic ratio. Relaxation gaps compare the integral optimum with a relaxation lower bound, while locality gaps compare the worst local optimum with the global optimum.

children.title: Formulation Gaps versus Computational Hardness
children.top_down_role: The boundary between method-specific limitations and general algorithmic lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between exact linear-formulation lower bounds and algorithm-independent computational hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_n\) be an exact solution polytope for an optimization family. A superpolynomial lower bound on its linear extension complexity \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)\) rules out polynomial-size exact linear extended formulations projecting to \(P_n\). It does not rule out polynomial-time optimization by combinatorial, dynamic-programming, semidefinite, oracle, or other non-LP methods. Such a formulation lower bound becomes a computational lower bound only after the permitted algorithmic model is restricted or an independent complexity reduction is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large linear extension complexity excludes small exact LP formulations, not all efficient algorithms for the underlying optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(P_n\) is the convex hull of the relevant feasible solutions.
Extension complexity counts inequalities in exact linear extended formulations.

notation.meaning: exact solution polytope at size n

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation-Size Lower Bounds Are Model-Specific

assumptions_latex: The separating example is a minimization problem with \(n\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A formulation or locality gap, without an algorithm-independent reduction or lower-bound argument, does not imply approximation hardness for the underlying optimization problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between formulation-specific or neighborhood-specific gaps and algorithmic inapproximability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integrality gap limits approximation guarantees certified solely by comparison with the specified relaxation value; it does not by itself lower-bound every algorithm for the underlying problem. Likewise, a locality gap exhibits poor locally optimal solutions for the specified neighborhood, but it does not show that every algorithm using that neighborhood must return one of them. For example, let the sole integral feasible solution be \(\mathbf1\in\{0,1\}^n\) with objective \(\sum_i x_i\), and relax to \(P_n=\{x\in[0,1]^n:\sum_i x_i\ge1\}\). The integral optimum is \(n\), the relaxation optimum is \(1\), and the integrality gap is \(n\), although the exact integral solution is produced immediately. General inapproximability requires a complexity-theoretic reduction or another algorithm-independent lower-bound argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large formulation gap limits what that relaxation value can certify, and a large locality gap exposes poor local optima. Neither fact alone proves that the underlying problem is computationally hard to approximate.
knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Gaps versus Computational Hardness

children.title: Integrality Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limitations specific to optimization relaxations and formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal asymptotic refinement of constant, growing, and finite-size-infinite regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For size map \(s(I)\), define \(g_R(n)=\sup\{\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)/\operatorname{OPT}_R(I):I\in\mathcal I,\ s(I)\le n\}\) for minimization whenever the ratios are defined. Then \(g_R(n)\) is nondecreasing. The relaxation is exact when \(g_R(n)=1\) for all \(n\), has a constant gap when \(\sup_n g_R(n)<\infty\), has a growing size-dependent gap when every \(g_R(n)<\infty\) but \(g_R(n)\to\infty\), and has an infinite finite-size gap when \(g_R(n)=\infty\) for some \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone finite-size profile distinguishes exact, bounded, asymptotically growing, and already infinite gap regimes.
assumptions_latex: The conventional minimization ratio is defined on every compared instance.
\(s(I)\in\mathbb N\) is fixed.

notation.meaning: Worst integrality gap among instances of size at most n.

knowledge_statements.title: Size-Indexed Integrality-Gap Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary for multiplicative integrality-gap ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplicative gap ratio is not informative without compatible signs and a nonzero denominator. For minimization, if \(\operatorname{OPT}_R(I)=0<\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)\), the instance gap is infinite; if both optima are zero, the ratio \(0/0\) is undefined and requires a declared convention or an additive gap. Negative or sign-changing objectives require normalization before the standard ratio classification applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero or sign-changing optima can make a multiplicative integrality gap infinite or undefined.
assumptions_latex: Integral and relaxation optima are compared on the same instance.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Optimum and Sign Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality gaps belong to a specified formulation and instance class, not to the combinatorial problem alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1(I)\subseteq R_2(I)\) be two minimization relaxations containing the same integral feasible solutions. Then \(\operatorname{OPT}_{R_2}(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}_{R_1}(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)\), and hence \[\frac{\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)}{\operatorname{OPT}_{R_1}(I)}\le\frac{\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)}{\operatorname{OPT}_{R_2}(I)}.\] Thus strengthening a relaxation cannot worsen its conventional integrality gap. The analogous conclusion holds for maximization under the reversed ratio convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger relaxation has no larger integrality gap, so every gap claim must identify its formulation and instance class.
assumptions_latex: Both relaxations contain the same integral feasible solutions.
All compared optimum values are positive and finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Dependence of Integrality Gaps
Integrality Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case multiplicative regimes for minimization relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a class \(\mathcal I\) of minimization instances with positive finite integral and relaxation optima, define the integrality gap of relaxation \(R\) by \(\operatorname{gap}_R(\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)/\operatorname{OPT}_R(I)\). The regime is exact when this value is \(1\), constant when it is bounded independently of input size, size-dependent when the restriction to size-\(n\) instances grows with \(n\), and unbounded when the supremum is infinite. For maximization, the ratio is reversed so that every gap is at least \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality-gap regimes classify the worst ratio between integral and relaxed optima as exact, constant, size-dependent, or unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\operatorname{OPT}_R(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}_I(I)<\infty\) for minimization instances.

children.title: Locality Gap Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case loss of locally optimal solutions for a maximization problem under a fixed feasible neighborhood system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, let \(L_N(I)=\{x:c_I(x)\ge c_I(z)\text{ for every }z\in N_I(x)\}\). Assume \(L_N(I)\ne\varnothing\) and \(0<c_I(x)\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)<\infty\) for every \(x\in L_N(I)\). Define \[\operatorname{lgap}^{\max}_N(\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_{x\in L_N(I)}\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}{c_I(x)}.\] If \(N_I(x)\subseteq N'_I(x)\) for every \(I,x\), then \(L_{N'}(I)\subseteq L_N(I)\) and \(\operatorname{lgap}^{\max}_{N'}(\mathcal I)\le\operatorname{lgap}^{\max}_N(\mathcal I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For maximization, the locality gap is the optimum divided by the local-optimum value; enlarging every neighborhood cannot increase it.

children.title: Local Charging Schemes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent representation of positive sender costs as cost-weighted fractional associations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(A,O;E)\) be a finite allowed-association graph and suppose \(c(a)>0\) for every \(a\in A\). A charge allocation supported on \(E\) satisfies \(\sum_{o:ao\in E}q(a,o)=c(a)\) exactly when there are coefficients \(p_{ao}\ge0\), zero off \(E\), such that \(\sum_{o\in O}p_{ao}=1\) and \(q(a,o)=c(a)p_{ao}\). Under this normalization, the receiver conditions become \[\sum_{a\in A}c(a)p_{ao}\le\alpha c(o)\quad(o\in O).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive sender costs, a local charging scheme is equivalently a probability distribution of each sender's cost over its allowed comparator associations.

Local Charging Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local charge allocation certifying a multiplicative comparison between two finite nonnegative combinatorial solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(O\) be finite sets of objects with nonnegative costs, where \(c(A)=\sum_{a\in A}c(a)\) and \(c(O)=\sum_{o\in O}c(o)\), and let \(\alpha\ge 0\). A local \(\alpha\)-charging certificate is a function \(q:A\times O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) satisfying \(\sum_{o\in O}q(a,o)=c(a)\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\sum_{a\in A}q(a,o)\le \alpha c(o)\) for every \(o\in O\). Consequently, \[c(A)=\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{o\in O}q(a,o)\le \alpha c(O).\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global accounting when local charges need not recover each candidate cost exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,O\) be finite, let \(q:A\times O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), define \(L(o)=\sum_{a\in A}q(a,o)\), and define \(\delta(a)=c(a)-\sum_{o\in O}q(a,o)\). Then \[c(A)=\sum_{o\in O}L(o)+\sum_{a\in A}\delta(a).\] If additionally \(c(o)\ge0\), \(\alpha\ge0\), and \(L(o)\le\alpha c(o)\) for every \(o\), then \[c(A)\le\alpha c(O)+\sum_{a\in A}\delta(a).\] Consequently, nonpositive total deficit—and in particular senderwise overcoverage—preserves \(c(A)\le\alpha c(O)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(O\) be finite sets, let \(q:A\times O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), define \(c(A)=\sum_{a\in A}c(a)\), and define \(L(o)=\sum_{a\in A}q(a,o)\). If \(c(a)=\sum_{o\in O}q(a,o)\) for every \(a\in A\), then \[c(A)=\sum_{a\in A}c(a)=\sum_{o\in O}L(o).\] Hence any bound \(\sum_{o\in O}L(o)\le B(O)\) implies \(c(A)\le B(O)\). In particular, if \(c(o)\ge0\), \(c(O)=\sum_{o\in O}c(o)\), \(\alpha\ge0\), and \(L(o)\le\alpha c(o)\) for every \(o\in O\), then \(c(A)\le\alpha c(O)\).

children.title: Charge-Congestion Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp feasibility threshold for distributing prescribed nonnegative charges through an allowed incidence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(A,O;E)\) be a finite bipartite graph, with demands \(d:A\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), capacities \(c:O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), and \(\alpha\ge0\). There exists \(q:E\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) satisfying \(\sum_{o:ao\in E}q(a,o)=d(a)\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\sum_{a:ao\in E}q(a,o)\le\alpha c(o)\) for every \(o\in O\) if and only if \[d(S)\le\alpha c(N_G(S))\quad\text{for every }S\subseteq A.\] If \(d(A)=0\), the least congestion is \(0\). Otherwise, if \(c(N_G(S))>0\) for every \(S\) with \(d(S)>0\), the least congestion is \[\alpha^*=\max_{S\subseteq A:\,d(S)>0}\frac{d(S)}{c(N_G(S))}.\] If some \(S\) has \(d(S)>0=c(N_G(S))\), no finite congestion factor exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-restricted fractional charging scheme exists exactly when every sender subset has enough neighboring capacity; the worst demand-to-neighbor-capacity ratio is the sharp congestion factor.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The sharp approximation factor attainable by a fixed finite nonnegative charge allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(O\) be finite sets, let \(q:A\times O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), and let \(c:O\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Under this condition, the least admissible factor is \[\alpha^*=\max_{o\in O:\,c(o)>0}\frac{L(o)}{c(o)}.\] If \(m\) unit-load candidate objects charge a single unit-cost comparator object, then \(\alpha^*=m\), so that allocation cannot certify a smaller factor.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange Arguments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A weighted maximization certificate derived from feasible one-for-many exchanges and bounded witness multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,O\) belong to a feasible family and have nonnegative additive weight \(w\). For every \(o\in O\setminus A\), suppose there is \(X_o\subseteq A\setminus O\) such that \((A\setminus X_o)\cup\{o\}\) is feasible. If local optimality yields \(w(o)\le\sum_{a\in X_o}w(a)\), and every \(a\in A\setminus O\) belongs to at most \(k\) sets \(X_o\), where \(k\ge1\), then \[w(O\setminus A)\le k w(A\setminus O),\qquad w(O)\le k w(A).\] Thus the exchange family and its multiplicities certify a \(k\)-approximation for maximization.

The map \(\varphi\), together with the pointwise inequalities, is directly checkable as an approximation certificate.

children.title: Potential-Function Comparisons

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint condition required when the terminal potential is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact telescoped bound contains \(-\Phi_T\). Replacing it by \(0\) requires \(\Phi_T\ge0\), or more generally a known lower bound on \(\Phi_T\). Without one, take \(T=1\), \(\alpha=b_0=\Phi_0=0\), \(\Phi_1=-1\), and \(\ell_0=1\): the local inequality holds, but \(\ell_0\le\alpha b_0+\Phi_0\) fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal potential may be discarded only when it has a suitable lower bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Telescoping with transition-dependent comparison multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell_t\le\alpha_t b_t+\Phi_t-\Phi_{t+1}\) for every \(t<T\), then \[\sum_{t<T}\ell_t\le\sum_{t<T}\alpha_t b_t+\Phi_0-\Phi_T.\] If \(b_t\ge0\), \(\alpha_t\le\bar\alpha\), and \(\Phi_T\ge0\), this implies \(\sum_{t<T}\ell_t\le\bar\alpha\sum_{t<T}b_t+\Phi_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition-dependent factors telescope exactly; a uniform upper bound on them yields a uniform global factor.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A telescoping potential comparison that converts transitionwise inequalities into a global quality bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For transitions \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), let \(\ell_t,b_t\ge0\) and let the potential satisfy \(\Phi_t\ge0\). If, for a constant \(\alpha\ge0\), every transition obeys \[\ell_t\le\alpha b_t+\Phi_t-\Phi_{t+1},\] then summation telescopes to \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ell_t\le\alpha\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t+\Phi_0-\Phi_T\le\alpha\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t+\Phi_0.\] Thus local losses may exceed their benchmark charges when the excess is paid by a decrease in potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A potential decrease pays for local excess loss, and telescoping leaves only the initial and final potentials in the global comparison.

children.title: Amortized Loss Accounting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on discarding the endpoint term in amortized loss bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), take \(T=1\), \(\ell_0=M\), \(\Phi_0=0\), and \(\Phi_1=-M\). Then \(\widehat\ell_0=\ell_0+\Phi_1-\Phi_0=0\), while the actual loss is \(M\). Thus a bound on total amortized loss alone gives no bound on total actual loss unless \(\Phi_0-\Phi_T\) is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A potential may pay for arbitrary actual loss by ending sufficiently negative, so the endpoint correction or a terminal lower bound is essential.
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint-Potential Correction Is Necessary
Amortized Loss Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting identity relating actual loss, potential change, and amortized loss over a finite execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(\ell_t,b_t\in\mathbb R\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), and let \(\Phi_t\in\mathbb R\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T\). Define \(\widehat\ell_t=\ell_t+\Phi_{t+1}-\Phi_t\). Then \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\widehat\ell_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ell_t+\Phi_T-\Phi_0.\] If \(\widehat\ell_t\le\alpha b_t\) for every \(t\), then \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ell_t\le\alpha\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b_t+\Phi_0-\Phi_T.\] In particular, when \(\Phi_0=0\) and \(\Phi_T\ge0\), total actual loss is at most \(\alpha\) times total benchmark charge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the potential change to each actual loss defines amortized loss; telescoping converts local amortized bounds into a global bound, including the multiplicative factor alpha.

\(\alpha\ge0\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between a potential-drop comparison and a pointwise amortized-loss bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix sequences \(\ell_t,b_t,\Phi_t\) and define \(\widehat\ell_t=\ell_t+\Phi_{t+1}-\Phi_t\). For every transition \(t\), the potential inequality and amortized inequality are algebraically equivalent: \[\ell_t\le\alpha b_t+\Phi_t-\Phi_{t+1}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\widehat\ell_t\le\alpha b_t.\] Consequently, specifying a potential that proves the left-hand inequalities is equivalent to specifying amortized losses satisfying the right-hand bounds, provided the amortized losses use the displayed potential-change convention. Both representations yield the same telescoping global comparison.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic recovery of an outcome meeting an expectation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let integrable cost \(C\) be determined by random choices \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\). After fixing \(Z_1=z_1,\ldots,Z_{i-1}=z_{i-1}\), choose a positive-conditional-probability value \(z_i\) minimizing \(\mathbb E[C\mid Z_1=z_1,\ldots,Z_i=z_i]\). After all choices are fixed, the resulting minimization solution satisfies \(C(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\le\mathbb E[C]\). Maximizing conditional expectation gives the analogous maximization statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization counterpart and the existential consequence of an expectation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a randomized maximization algorithm returning \(0\le V_I\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), an expected \(\alpha\)-approximation, \(0<\alpha\le1\), satisfies \(\mathbb E[V_I]\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(I)\). If the output distribution has finite support, some supported output has value at least \(\mathbb E[V_I]\), hence at least \(\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(I)\). For minimization, some supported outcome has cost at most its expectation.

\(0<\alpha\le1\) for maximization

Expectation-Based Quality Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected approximation quality for a randomized minimization algorithm, with its basic tail conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization instance \(I\), let \(C_I\ge0\) almost surely be the random cost returned by an algorithm, let \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)>0\), and let \(\alpha\ge0\). The algorithm has expected approximation factor \(\alpha\) on \(I\) when \[\mathbb E[C_I]\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(I).\] If \(C_I=\sum_{j=1}^m Y_j\) for finitely many integrable random variables \(Y_j\), then \(\mathbb E[C_I]=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E[Y_j]\), without any independence assumption. Moreover, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), Markov's inequality gives \[\Pr\!\left(C_I>\frac{\alpha}{\delta}\operatorname{OPT}(I)\right)\le\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected output cost defines expected approximation quality; finite integrable decompositions may be analyzed by linearity of expectation, and Markov's inequality gives a weak tail guarantee without independence.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent Bernoulli variables satisfy \(X=\sum_iX_i\) and \(\mu=\mathbb EX\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \[\Pr(X\le(1-\varepsilon)\mu)\le e^{-\varepsilon^2\mu/2},\qquad \Pr(X\ge(1+\varepsilon)\mu)\le e^{-\varepsilon^2\mu/3}.\]

\(0<\varepsilon<1\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoeffding Inequality for Independent Bounded Summands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive concentration for independent variables with bounded ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent and \(a_i\le X_i\le b_i\) almost surely, then for \(S=\sum_iX_i\) and \(t>0\), \[\Pr(S-\mathbb ES\ge t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_i(b_i-a_i)^2}\right),\quad \Pr(|S-\mathbb ES|\ge t)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_i(b_i-a_i)^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bounded summands have sub-Gaussian additive tails controlled by their squared ranges.
assumptions_latex: The \(X_i\) are independent
\(a_i\le X_i\le b_i\) almost surely

Concentration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-input bounded-differences regime converting expected quality into additive high-probability quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent random variables, and let \(C=f(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) be integrable. Suppose constants \(c_1,ldots,c_n\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2>0\), and changing only coordinate \(i\) changes \(f\) by at most \(c_i\). Then, for every \(t>0\), \[\Pr(C-\mathbb E[C]\ge t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2}\right).\] Hence, if \(\alpha\ge0\), \(\operatorname{OPT}\ge0\), and \(\mathbb E[C]\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\), then for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[C\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}+\sqrt{\frac12\left(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2\right)\log\frac1\delta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent inputs and bounded coordinate influence yield sub-Gaussian concentration, upgrading an expected objective bound to an additive high-probability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent
\(C=f(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) is integrable
\(|f(x)-f(x')|\le c_i\) whenever only coordinate \(i\) differs
\(c_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i c_i^2>0\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge2\), let \(C=m\) with probability \(1/m\) and \(C=0\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb E C=1\) while \(\Pr(C=m)=1/m\).

children.title: Dependency-Sensitive Probabilistic Analysis
children.top_down_role: Quality analysis when random choices are correlated or only partially independent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrary Dependence Defeats Independent Chernoff Tails
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of independent-sum concentration under perfect positive correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and set \(X_i=Z\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Then \(S=nZ\), \(\mathbb ES=n/2\), and \(\Pr(S=n)=1/2\). Thus bounded Bernoulli marginals alone do not imply an exponentially small upper tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated indicators need not concentrate around their sum's mean.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Dependence Defeats Independent Chernoff Tails

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev concentration under pairwise rather than mutual independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are pairwise independent with finite variances and \(S=\sum_iX_i\), then \(\operatorname{Var}(S)=\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i)\). Hence for \(t>0\), \[\Pr(|S-\mathbb ES|\ge t)\le\frac{\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i)}{t^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise independence suffices for variance additivity and a Chebyshev tail, but not generally for Chernoff tails.
assumptions_latex: The \(X_i\) are pairwise independent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale concentration accommodating dependent random choices through bounded conditional increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_i)_{i=0}^n\) be a filtration and let \((M_i)_{i=0}^n\) be an integrable martingale adapted to it. If constants \(c_i\ge0\) satisfy \(|M_i-M_{i-1}|\le c_i\) almost surely for each \(i=1,\ldots,n\), then, for every \(t>0\), \[\Pr(M_n-M_0\ge t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2}\right),\] provided \(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2>0\). In particular, let \(C\) be integrable and \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable, let \(\mathcal F_0\) be trivial, and define \(M_i=\mathbb E[C\mid\mathcal F_i]\). Then \(M_0=\mathbb E[C]\) and \(M_n=C\) almost surely. Consequently, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[C\le\mathbb E[C]+\sqrt{2\left(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2\right)\log\frac1\delta}.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between k-wise and full independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let U_1,\ldots,U_k be independent uniform bits and set U_{k+1}=U_1\oplus\cdots\oplus U_k. Then U_1,\ldots,U_{k+1} are k-wise independent but not (k+1)-wise independent, because U_1\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{k+1}=0 with probability one.

knowledge_statements.title: k-Wise Independence Need Not Extend

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and uniform finite-range specialization of limited independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Random variables X_1,\ldots,X_n are k-wise independent if every subfamily X_{i_1},\ldots,X_{i_r} with r\le k has product distribution. Equivalently, for all values a_1,\ldots,a_r, \Pr[X_{i_1}=a_1,\ldots,X_{i_r}=a_r]=\prod_{j=1}^r\Pr[X_{i_j}=a_j]. If all variables are uniform on a common finite set D, every such r-tuple is therefore uniform on D^r.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every subfamily of at most k variables behaves exactly as an independent product family.
assumptions_latex: 1\le k\le n.
The displayed point-probability formulation is for discrete finite-range variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact k-Wise Independence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-seed construction of uniform k-wise independent field-valued variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q be a prime power and 1\le k\le n\le q. Choose distinct t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathbb F_q and a uniformly random coefficient vector (A_0,\ldots,A_{k-1})\in\mathbb F_q^k. With P(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}A_jt^j and X_i=P(t_i), every r\le k distinct evaluations form a uniform vector in \mathbb F_q^r. The seed space has q^k elements and entropy k\log_2 q bits; it is encoded by k field elements. Exactly k\log_2q unbiased bits suffice when q is a power of two, while other q require an explicitly specified exact field-sampling model rather than the bound k\lceil\log_2q\rceil.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating a uniformly seeded polynomial of degree below k at distinct field points produces uniform k-wise independent variables from k field elements.

1\le k\le n\le q.
t_1,\ldots,t_n are distinct.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic bad-event avoidance using a dominating potential on reachable prefixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B be determined by finite random choices X_1,\ldots,X_m. For each reachable positive-probability prefix p, let \Phi(p)\ge0 satisfy \Pr(B\mid p)\le\Phi(p). Assume \Phi(\varnothing)<1 and that every nonterminal reachable prefix p has a supported child p\circ a with \Phi(p\circ a)\le\Phi(p). Repeatedly choose such a child. The resulting complete assignment \omega satisfies \Phi(\omega)<1 and hence \omega\notin B, since a complete assignment in B would have conditional failure probability one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominating estimator that starts below one and never increases along a supported completion certifies a deterministic outcome outside the bad event.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Order Marginals Preserve Only Low-Degree Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on substituting k-wise independence for full independence in an estimator analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two distributions on finitely many coordinates agree on every joint marginal involving at most k coordinates, they give the same expectation to every multilinear polynomial of degree at most k in coordinate-indicator variables. They need not agree on events or tests involving more than k coordinates. Consequently, an estimator proved valid under full independence is not automatically valid under a k-wise independent surrogate; its domination and seed-conditioning properties must be re-established for that surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching k-coordinate marginals preserves low-degree moment calculations, not arbitrary global events or conditional estimators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of fixed positive gap thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C>S>0\) and \(\lambda>0\), replacing \((C,S)\) by \((\lambda C,\lambda S)\) preserves the multiplicative gap because \((\lambda C)/(\lambda S)=C/S\). A common additive shift generally does not preserve this ratio.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a fixed maximization promise gap into a constant-factor lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose target instances satisfy the promise \(\operatorname{OPT}\ge C\) or \(\operatorname{OPT}\le S\), where \(C>S>0\). Any polynomial-time maximization algorithm with ratio \(r<C/S\) distinguishes the cases by testing whether its feasible output value exceeds \(S\). Thus NP-hardness of the promise distinction excludes every such \(r\)-approximation unless \(P=NP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NP-hard fixed maximization gap of ratio C/S rules out every approximation factor strictly better than C/S.
assumptions_latex: The objective is nonnegative and maximized.

Constant-Gap Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Many-one reductions preserving a fixed multiplicative promise gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization problems with nonnegative objectives, a constant-gap reduction maps each instance \(x\) in polynomial time to an instance \(f(x)\) and fixes constants \(C>S>0\), independent of \(|x|\), such that \[\operatorname{OPT}(x)\geq Y(x)\implies\operatorname{OPT}(f(x))\geq C,\qquad \operatorname{OPT}(x)\leq N(x)\implies\operatorname{OPT}(f(x))\leq S.\] The target promise therefore has multiplicative gap \(C/S>1\). A solution or decision procedure distinguishing the target cases must be transformable in polynomial time into one distinguishing the source cases. For minimization, interchange the threshold directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-gap reduction maps promised instances to target instances whose completeness and soundness thresholds differ by a fixed ratio greater than one.
assumptions_latex: Objectives and thresholds are nonnegative.
The instance and answer transformations run in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target promise has a size-independent gap \(C/S>1\) and preserves source-case distinguishability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating bounded-gap from genuinely asymptotic gap amplification.

The constant-gap regime is characterized by \(g(N(n))=O(1)\); the growing-gap regime requires \(g(N(n))\to\infty\). Consequently, an unbounded formal function \(g(N)\) does not yield growing-gap hardness unless it is unbounded on the sizes actually produced by the reduction. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard L-reduction between nonnegative optimization problems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical failures of verifier–constraint fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reweighting two verifier tests from probabilities \((p,1-p)\) to \((p',1-p')\) changes the value of any assignment satisfying exactly one test whenever \(p'\ne p\), and can change the optimum. Separately, replacing one shared proof location by independent local variables permits inconsistent local assignments; two constraints requiring opposite values of the original location then become simultaneously satisfiable after duplication although no original proof satisfies both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing test weights distorts acceptance values, while duplicating a shared proof position without equality constraints can raise the encoded optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{distribution mismatch or missing consistency constraints can destroy value and gap fidelity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight and Consistency Distortion Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes per-assignment, optimum-value, gap, and reduction fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a verifier value \(A_x(\pi)\) and encoded constraint value \(B_x(\phi(\pi))\), per-assignment fidelity requires equality for every \(\pi\); optimum fidelity requires only equality of the two maxima; gap fidelity requires preservation of the promised yes- and no-instance thresholds; reduction fidelity additionally requires polynomial-time construction and polynomial encoded size. Per-assignment fidelity implies optimum fidelity, and uniform threshold preservation implies gap fidelity, but the converses need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact agreement for every proof is stronger than preserving only the optimum or promise gap, and hardness transfer additionally requires a polynomial-time, polynomial-size encoding.
assumptions_latex: The assignment map \(\phi\) and the compared value functions are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{per-assignment fidelity}\Rightarrow\text{optimum fidelity};\quad\text{value fidelity plus polynomial construction}\Rightarrow\text{reduction fidelity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy of Encoding Fidelity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates semantic value preservation from approximation-hardness transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even an exactly value-preserving encoding does not constitute a polynomial-time hardness reduction when construction time, constraint count, predicate descriptions, variable indices, alphabet encoding, or numerical weights have superpolynomial total length. Conversely, polynomial size without the required value or gap correspondence does not preserve an approximation frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hardness transfer requires both value or gap fidelity and polynomial construction size; neither condition alone is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Reduction Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate fidelity certificate and its effect on optimum and promise thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If assignments correspond in both directions without increasing distortion and \(|A_x(\pi)-B_x(\phi(\pi))|\le\eta\) uniformly, then the two optimum values differ by at most \(\eta\). Consequently a verifier promise \(A_x^*\ge c\) on yes-instances and \(A_x^*\le s\) on no-instances becomes \(B_x^*\ge c-\eta\) and \(B_x^*\le s+\eta\); a positive encoded gap is guaranteed only when \(c-s>2\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform η value distortion changes each optimum by at most η and preserves a positive completeness–soundness gap only when the original gap exceeds 2η.
assumptions_latex: Assignments have value-preserving correspondences in both directions up to \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Value-Distortion Bound
Encoding-Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which verifier–constraint conversion preserves the acceptance gap exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The verifier–constraint correspondence is value preserving only when the encoded constraints retain the verifier's randomness distribution, query consistency, and acceptance predicates. If random string \(r\) receives weight \(\Pr[r]\), then every proof \(\pi\) has identical verifier and constraint values. Replacing these weights by another distribution, duplicating proof locations without consistency constraints, or approximating predicates can change the optimum and hence the completeness–soundness gap. Exact fidelity is certified by \[\operatorname{Val}(I_x,\pi)=\Pr_r[V^\pi(x;r)=1]\quad\text{for every }\pi.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The encoding preserves a PCP gap exactly only when every proof has the same acceptance value and constraint-system value.
assumptions_latex: Verifier randomness and constraint weights are represented exactly.
Shared proof positions remain globally consistent.

notation.meaning: constraint instance encoded from verifier input x
satisfied constraint weight under assignment pi

review_flags: The precise fidelity boundary depends on the chosen PCP-to-CSP encoding and requires a supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the container, and equality for every proof is a suitable exact-fidelity certificate. The listed failure modes depend on the precise verifier-to-constraint construction and need an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: PCP Gap-Transformation Calculus
children.top_down_role: High-level hardness mechanisms inherited from proof-system constructions.

children.title: PCP Composition
children.top_down_role: Hardness interfaces arising from composition of probabilistic proof systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Executable composition procedure for the robust global-encoding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sample the outer verifier's random string, identify its requested proof positions, run the inner decoder for every requested position against the global encoded proof, and apply the outer acceptance predicate to the decoded symbols. Shared inner queries may be cached but do not alter the worst-case bound \(q_oq_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition samples an outer test, decodes each requested outer symbol from one global encoded proof, and evaluates the original outer predicate.
assumptions_latex: The inner decoder exposes the symbol alphabet required by the outer predicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Query Replacement Procedure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a single globally consistent decoded outer proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If different outer tests may decode mutually inconsistent values for the same outer proof position, high inner acceptance need not define any global outer proof. Consequently outer soundness cannot be invoked, and locally satisfiable inner views can all accept even though every globally consistent outer proof is rejected with the promised probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally successful inner proofs do not preserve outer soundness unless their answers agree with one global outer proof.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{local decoding without global agreement}\not\Rightarrow s_{\mathrm{comp}}\le s_o+o(1).
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Acceptance Without Global Agreement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A precise outer–inner composition law under a global decoding guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an outer verifier query at most \(q_o\) symbols of a proof \(\pi\), have completeness \(c_o\), soundness \(s_o\), and use \(r_o\) random bits. Encode \(\pi\) globally. Suppose an inner local decoder uses \(r_i\) fresh random bits and \(q_i\) encoded-proof queries per requested symbol, and for every encoded proof there exists one global \(\pi\) such that each decoded requested symbol is incorrect with probability at most \(\eta\). Simulating all outer queries then gives completeness at least \(c_o-q_o\eta\), soundness at most \(s_o+q_o\eta\), query complexity at most \(q_oq_i\), and randomness at most \(r_o+q_or_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all inner decodings are close to one global outer proof, a union bound transfers outer completeness and soundness with additive qη error and multiplies query cost.
assumptions_latex: The encoded proof admits a single global decoded proof \(\pi\).
Each requested symbol has decoding error at most \(\eta\).
Inner random strings are fresh conditional on the outer randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_{\mathrm{comp}}\ge c_o-q_o\eta,\quad s_{\mathrm{comp}}\le s_o+q_o\eta,\quad q_{\mathrm{comp}}\le q_oq_i,\quad r_{\mathrm{comp}}\le r_o+q_or_i.

notation.meaning: inner decoder resource parameters per symbol

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Global-Encoding Composition
PCP Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer–inner verifier composition with multiplicative query cost and controlled completeness and soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an outer verifier have completeness \(c_o\), soundness \(s_o\), and query complexity \(q_o\). Suppose each outer local acceptance test is verified by an inner PCP with completeness \(c_i\), soundness \(s_i\), and query complexity \(q_i\), using an encoding consistent across outer answers. The composed verifier simulates the outer randomness and invokes the inner verifier on the selected test. Its query complexity is at most \(q_oq_i\), its completeness is at least \(c_oc_i\), and its soundness is bounded by a function determined by \(s_o,s_i\) and the agreement guarantee of the encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PCP composition replaces each outer test by an inner verifier, trading multiplied query cost for combined completeness and soundness parameters.
assumptions_latex: The inner encoding is consistent across overlapping outer tests.
The inner soundness analysis supplies the required agreement or decoding guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\mathrm{comp}}\le q_oq_i\), \(c_{\mathrm{comp}}\ge c_oc_i\), with \(s_{\mathrm{comp}}\) controlled by \(s_o,s_i\) and agreement
review_flags: PCP composition has several incompatible parameter theorems; the path does not determine a sharper soundness formula.
An authoritative composition theorem and locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A composition principle fits the PCP Composition container, but the statement does not identify a concrete composition theorem and leaves the soundness conclusion as an unspecified function of parameters and agreement. Different PCP composition frameworks have materially different hypotheses and bounds, so an authoritative theorem and locator are required.

children.title: Gap Amplification
children.top_down_role: Hardness interfaces that enlarge completeness–soundness separation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifier transformation that strengthens acceptance-probability separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A gap-amplification transformation maps a verifier with completeness \(c\) and soundness \(s<c\) to one with parameters \((c',s')\) whose separation is stronger under a declared criterion, such as smaller soundness at preserved completeness or smaller two-sided error, while explicitly accounting for randomness, queries, proof length, alphabet, and construction size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap amplification strengthens a declared completeness–soundness criterion and must report the verifier-resource cost.
assumptions_latex: The amplification criterion and verifier model are fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Completeness–Soundness Amplification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failures of elementary repetition formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Product and concentration bounds require independent trials. If every repeated run uses the same random string, all outcomes can coincide and repetition need not reduce soundness. Moreover, an AND rule lowers completeness to a power when completeness is imperfect, while a threshold \(\tau\notin(s,c)\) cannot simultaneously drive completeness error and soundness to zero by the stated concentration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated runs may provide no amplification, AND repetition loses imperfect completeness, and a threshold outside the original gap cannot amplify both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{independence and }s<\tau<c\text{ are essential to the stated exponential bounds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Independence and Threshold Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided amplification by majority or another fixed threshold; distinct from the deferred all-accept repetition seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Execute \(t\) independent runs and accept when at least \(\tau t\) runs accept, where \(s<\tau<c\). Then completeness is at least \(1-\exp(-2t(c-\tau)^2)\), soundness is at most \(\exp(-2t(\tau-s)^2)\), randomness is \(tr\), and queries are at most \(tq\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent threshold vote exponentially suppresses both completeness error and soundness when the threshold lies strictly between soundness and completeness.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le s<\tau<c\le1\).
The \(t\) executions use independent random strings.
The same proof is tested in every execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_t\ge1-e^{-2t(c-\tau)^2},\quad s_t\le e^{-2t(\tau-s)^2},\quad r_t=tr,\quad q_t\le tq.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Threshold-Repetition Bound
Gap Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent repetition of a probabilistic verifier, including its parameter costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let verifier \(V\) have completeness at least \(c\), soundness at most \(s<c\), randomness complexity \(r\), and query complexity \(q\). Define \(V^{\wedge t}\) to execute \(t\) independent runs of \(V\) and accept exactly when every run accepts. For every fixed proof, independence gives acceptance probability equal to the product of the runwise probabilities. Consequently, \(V^{\wedge t}\) has completeness at least \(c^t\), soundness at most \(s^t\), randomness complexity \(tr\), and query complexity at most \(tq\). In particular, perfect completeness is preserved when \(c=1\), while soundness decreases exponentially in \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent AND-repetition raises completeness and soundness to the repetition power, exponentially reducing soundness while multiplying randomness and queries by the repetition count.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le s<c\le1\) and \(t\in\mathbb N\).
The \(t\) verifier runs use mutually independent random strings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(V^{\wedge t})\ge c^t,\quad s(V^{\wedge t})\le s^t,\quad r_t=tr,\quad q_t\le tq.\)

notation.meaning: The AND of t independent executions of V.
